dwa_title: Proofread documents, records, or other files to ensure accuracy.
rationale: Grammar, consistency and data-accuracy checking against source records is exactly what deployed text tools already do end-to-end; residual human involvement is stylistic preference, not capability.

dwa_title: Retrieve information from electronic sources.
rationale: Querying databases and search systems is the canonical case of software doing the whole task; the only residual is judging source reliability.

dwa_title: Edit written materials.
rationale: Text revision for grammar, clarity and style is the canonical LLM strength and is already shipped in mainstream writing tools; only high-stakes voice and factual verification still pull a human back in.

dwa_title: Format digital documents, data, or images.
rationale: Formatting is rule-driven transformation of digital artefacts, well covered by templates, scripts and multimodal models, and mistakes are trivially reversible.

dwa_title: Search files, databases or reference materials to obtain needed information.
rationale: Retrieval over indexed digital corpora is the canonical strength of search plus RAG systems; the only friction is non-digitised or access-restricted material.

dwa_title: Edit documents.
rationale: Document editing is language transformation over supplied text, fully within deployed model capability; residual human need is limited to final responsibility for contractual or regulated wording.

dwa_title: Read documents to gather technical information.
rationale: This is pure information extraction from text — the core competence of retrieval-augmented language models; only verification of citation fidelity keeps a human nearby.

dwa_title: Compile specialized bibliographies or lists of materials.
rationale: Catalogue search, citation management and LLM synthesis cover bibliography compilation well; the binding issue is relevance curation for a specific patron's need and source-verification against hallucination.

dwa_title: Update website content.
rationale: Content generation and CMS publishing are already scriptable and LLM-drafted; the binding constraint is editorial approval of what goes public under a brand's name, not the mechanics.

dwa_title: Prepare informational or reference materials.
rationale: This is essentially synthesis and exposition of existing information, which deployed language models perform end-to-end; only factual verification and house-style approval remain human.

dwa_title: Study product information to acquire professional knowledge.
rationale: Ingesting spec sheets and product literature is near-pure document comprehension, highly amenable to models; the constraint is that the worker must be able to recall and apply it live in front of a customer or on a job.

dwa_title: Review professional literature to maintain professional knowledge.
rationale: Retrieval, screening and summarisation of literature is already well served by deployed tools; the constraint is that the resulting knowledge must be internalised by the practitioner who will later apply it.

dwa_title: Enter information into databases or software programs.
rationale: OCR, document-extraction models and RPA now ingest most structured and semi-structured sources end-to-end; only messy or unverifiable source documents still require a keying human.

dwa_title: Create images or other visual displays.
rationale: Generic image and visual-display creation is precisely what deployed generative models do end-to-end; only client intent and rights clearance keep a person in the loop.

dwa_title: Analyze data to identify trends or relationships among variables.
rationale: Trend detection and correlation discovery are routinely performed end-to-end by deployed analytics and AutoML pipelines; the human residue is distinguishing spurious from meaningful relationships.

dwa_title: Write computer programming code.
rationale: Code generation is the paradigm case of LLM capability, but specification ambiguity, integration with existing systems and responsibility for shipped defects still bind a human author and reviewer.

dwa_title: Analyze website or related online data to track trends or usage.
rationale: Web analytics platforms already collect, segment, anomaly-detect and narrate usage trends automatically, and errors are cheap and reversible, so nothing binds a human to the loop.

dwa_title: Research topics in area of expertise.
rationale: Information gathering and synthesis is the archetypal LLM task with search tools; residual risk of fabricated or stale sources means an expert must verify before relying on the output.

dwa_title: Translate information for others.
rationale: Machine translation is a mature deployed technology handling most general-purpose language conversion end-to-end; certified legal, medical and literary translation remains human-signed for fidelity and liability.

dwa_title: Calculate weights, volumes or other characteristics of materials.
rationale: This is deterministic arithmetic over densities, geometry and material tables, already embedded in CAD and process-control software; nothing physical or contested binds it.

dwa_title: Classify materials according to standard systems.
rationale: Applying a fixed taxonomy to described items is a classic classification task well served by ML and LLMs; the residual constraint is only where the material must be physically inspected or handled to be categorized.

dwa_title: Code data or other information.
rationale: Classification against a codebook (medical, survey, taxonomic) is exactly what current models do well; the constraint is ambiguous edge cases and audit requirements in regulated coding like billing.

dwa_title: Prepare technical reports for internal use.
rationale: Internal-audience technical write-ups have low external liability and abundant structured source data, so model drafting plus light review can carry most of the task.

dwa_title: Develop content for sales presentations or other materials.
rationale: Generating persuasive copy, decks and supporting collateral from product and customer data is squarely what generative models already do end-to-end; the binding constraint is only access to accurate internal product/pricing facts and brand sign-off.

dwa_title: Prepare graphics or other visual representations of information.
rationale: Chart and infographic generation from data is a solved code-generation problem with deployed tooling; residual human role is taste and checking that the visual does not mislead.

dwa_title: Update computer database information.
rationale: Record updating is the archetypal rules-based transaction already handled by integrations, RPA and workflow automation; residual human work is exception handling and source verification.

dwa_title: Stay informed about current developments in field of specialization.
rationale: Automated alerting and summarisation pipelines already deliver field developments continuously; judging which developments matter for one's own practice, and absorbing them, remains the human's part.

dwa_title: Prepare tests.
rationale: Item generation aligned to standards is a core LLM strength; the remaining constraint is validity review and psychometric vetting of high-stakes items.

dwa_title: Schedule appointments.
rationale: Self-service booking platforms and voice/chat agents already complete appointment scheduling end-to-end; nothing in the task requires a human signature.

dwa_title: Update knowledge about emerging industry or technology trends.
rationale: Trend monitoring is largely automated scanning and synthesis of public information, but distinguishing durable signal from hype is a contested judgment call the human still owns.

dwa_title: Create databases to store electronic data.
rationale: Instantiating a database from a specification is scripted, reversible and routinely handled by templates, provisioning tools and code-generating assistants.

dwa_title: Develop training materials.
rationale: Generative models produce usable curricula, slides and assessments directly, so the remaining human role is needs analysis, organisational context and validating that the material actually changes behaviour.

dwa_title: Create technology-based learning materials.
rationale: Authoring tools plus generative text, image and voice cover most content production, but integration into an LMS, accessibility compliance and interaction design still require human assembly.

dwa_title: Advise customers on the use of products or services.
rationale: Product usage guidance is documented knowledge delivered conversationally, the canonical deployed use case for LLM assistants.

dwa_title: Update technical knowledge.
rationale: Technical documentation, release notes and standards are ideal LLM input, yet much technical currency is acquired through hands-on practice with the equipment or system and must be internalised by the practitioner.

dwa_title: Develop instructional materials.
rationale: Content generation and alignment to stated learning objectives are automatable; the constraint is contested pedagogical judgment about sequencing and fit to a particular learner population.

dwa_title: Compile data or documentation.
rationale: Generic collection and collation of documents and data is largely a retrieval-and-formatting task already handled by document management and LLM tooling.

dwa_title: Develop promotional materials.
rationale: Generative text and image tools already produce deployable promotional copy and creative at scale; the residual human role is brand judgment and legal review, and errors are cheap to correct.

dwa_title: Prepare operational progress or status reports.
rationale: Status and progress reporting is mostly aggregation of tracked metrics into prose, a task deployed dashboards and LLM summarisers perform end-to-end; only contested interpretations of slippage need a human.

dwa_title: Compile technical information or documentation.
rationale: LLMs excel at gathering, structuring and drafting technical documentation, but sourcing authoritative specifications from engineers and certifying correctness keeps a human owner.

dwa_title: Prepare data for analysis.
rationale: Cleaning, joining and reshaping data is highly code-generatable, but decisions about outliers, missingness and what counts as valid still shape downstream conclusions and need an analyst's sign-off.

dwa_title: Develop procedures for data entry or processing.
rationale: Data entry and processing workflows are rule-bound and highly documentable, so drafting them is well within model capability; constraints are mostly integration with legacy systems rather than reasoning.

dwa_title: Answer telephones to direct calls or provide information.
rationale: Call routing and canned information delivery is the most thoroughly automated communication task in existence, with IVR and now conversational voice agents commercially deployed end-to-end.

dwa_title: Prepare operational reports.
rationale: Operational reporting draws on instrumented system data, and BI pipelines plus generated narrative summaries already produce these routinely with minimal review.

dwa_title: Verify mathematical calculations.
rationale: Recomputation and cross-footing are deterministic and have been machine-performed for decades; the only residual need is identifying which figures matter and signing off.

dwa_title: Design websites or web applications.
rationale: Template and generative site builders already ship end-to-end for commodity cases; bespoke brand, accessibility and conversion judgment is what keeps a designer in the loop.

dwa_title: Analyze energy usage data.
rationale: Metering, building-management analytics and automated disaggregation already produce energy usage findings end-to-end; humans mainly choose which recommended retrofits to fund.

dwa_title: Develop diagrams or flow charts of system operation.
rationale: Diagramming is essentially structured text (Mermaid, PlantUML, BPMN) that frontier models generate reliably; the only real limit is accurately eliciting how the undocumented system actually behaves.

dwa_title: Prepare instruction manuals.
rationale: Models draft procedures well from specifications, but hands-on validation that the documented steps actually work, plus liability for safety warnings, anchors a human reviewer.

dwa_title: Process healthcare paperwork.
rationale: Document extraction, coding and claims workflows are already heavily automated in commercial RCM software; remaining friction is fragmented systems, payer exceptions and HIPAA-driven sign-off rather than cognitive difficulty.

dwa_title: Train others in computer interface or software use.
rationale: Software instruction is pure information transfer in the same medium the learner is already working in; interactive walkthroughs and conversational assistants already deliver it end-to-end for most users.

dwa_title: Recommend products or services to customers.
rationale: Recommender systems plus conversational agents already drive most retail suggestion at scale; only high-consideration or high-trust sales still hinge on a human relationship.

dwa_title: Calculate numerical data for medical activities.
rationale: Dose and formula calculations are deterministic and already embedded in calculators and pharmacy systems; the residual constraint is mandated independent human verification because arithmetic errors can be lethal.

dwa_title: Answer customer questions about goods or services.
rationale: Product and service Q&A is retrieval over a known knowledge base, which deployed LLM assistants handle end-to-end; the main constraint is liability for wrong answers in regulated categories.

dwa_title: Advise customers on technical or procedural issues.
rationale: Technical support diagnosis over text and voice is already widely automated with retrieval over documentation; escalation of novel or irate cases is the residual human slice.

dwa_title: Develop instructional objectives.
rationale: Writing measurable objectives aligned to standards and taxonomies is a highly templated text task that current models perform reliably; only local curricular approval remains human.

dwa_title: Provide technical support for software maintenance or use.
rationale: Deployed AI support agents already resolve a substantial share of software help requests end-to-end from documentation and logs; escalation for novel defects and irate users is the residual human slice.

dwa_title: Develop software or computer applications.
rationale: Code generation is the strongest current LLM capability and agentic tools now complete whole features, but requirement ambiguity, integration with legacy context and review for correctness still gate end-to-end autonomy.

dwa_title: Prepare research or technical reports.
rationale: Structuring, drafting and summarising results is squarely in frontier-model territory; the binding constraint is verified fidelity to underlying data and a human author accepting responsibility for conclusions.

dwa_title: Prepare analytical reports.
rationale: Analysis-to-narrative is the paradigm LLM task and templated analytics pipelines already auto-generate reports; interpretation choices and data validation still need human sign-off.

dwa_title: Modify software programs to improve performance.
rationale: Profiling data plus code gives a closed feedback loop that models exploit well; the limit is regression risk in large unfamiliar codebases, which still needs human review before merge.

dwa_title: Maintain knowledge of current developments in area of expertise.
rationale: Monitoring and digesting literature, standards and news is exactly what retrieval-plus-LLM pipelines do well, but the output is an internalised competence a licensed or accountable practitioner must actually hold and apply, not a deliverable a machine can own.

dwa_title: Write articles, books or other original materials in area of expertise.
rationale: Models generate fluent long-form prose but genuine originality, subject-matter authority and reputational authorship are the value being sold, so the expert's name and vetting remain load-bearing.

dwa_title: Provide customers with general information or assistance.
rationale: General enquiry handling is low-stakes, script-shaped and grounded in retrievable knowledge bases, which is exactly what current deployed assistants do reliably.

dwa_title: Analyze market research data.
rationale: Survey coding, segmentation and cross-tab analysis are already substantially tool-driven and LLM-tractable; the binding constraint is framing which commercial question the data actually answers and defending the inference to decision-makers.

dwa_title: Apply mathematical principles or statistical approaches to solve problems in scientific or applied fields.
rationale: Symbolic and statistical computation is machine-native, but selecting an appropriate model and validating that its assumptions hold for the physical or applied problem still requires expert framing.

dwa_title: Analyze market or customer related data.
rationale: Segmentation, churn scoring and cohort analysis over CRM data are commodity automated pipelines; residual human input is framing the business question and privacy compliance rather than the analysis itself.

dwa_title: Prepare technical or operational reports.
rationale: Operational reporting is often already auto-generated from instrumented systems; residual human role is anomaly interpretation and attesting to accuracy.

dwa_title: Conduct research to inform art, designs, or other work.
rationale: Reference gathering, visual and textual precedent search are precisely what retrieval-augmented models do well; what limits full automation is that the researcher's aesthetic intent shapes what counts as relevant material, and some source material must be experienced in situ.

dwa_title: Update professional knowledge.
rationale: Machines can curate and digest the source material at scale, but the purpose of the activity is to install knowledge in the human who will later exercise it unaided.

dwa_title: Compile operational data.
rationale: Operational data aggregation is the core use case of ETL pipelines and BI reporting; the remaining friction is integrating unstructured or manually captured sources.

dwa_title: Manage documentation to ensure organization or accuracy.
rationale: Document classification, version control and completeness checking are well served by content-management systems plus LLM extraction; residual human role is attesting to accuracy in regulated records.

dwa_title: Review technical documents to plan work.
rationale: The reading half is highly exposed, but converting documents into an actual work plan requires site- and crew-specific context that is not in the documents.

dwa_title: Prepare proposal documents.
rationale: Document assembly from templates and prior content is largely automatable; the binding constraint is that the substantive offer and its accuracy still need human commitment.

dwa_title: Analyze operational or research data.
rationale: Generic data analysis is squarely in the wheelhouse of code-writing models and statistical tooling; framing the question and validating that results mean something remain human-owned.

dwa_title: Prepare scientific or technical reports or presentations.
rationale: Text and slide production from data is largely model-doable; hallucination risk and authorship accountability keep a scientist in the loop for verification.

dwa_title: Check data for recording errors.
rationale: Detecting transcription and recording errors is a pattern-matching task that validation rules, double-entry checks and models perform reliably and cheaply.

dwa_title: Maintain current knowledge related to work activities.
rationale: Heterogeneous activity spanning document reading and hands-on familiarity; tools can supply the information stream but the knowledge must end up in the worker performing the downstream tasks.

dwa_title: Review customer insurance information.
rationale: Coverage and eligibility verification runs against structured policy databases with established clearinghouse automation; exceptions and customer explanation are the shrinking human remainder.

dwa_title: Analyze operational data to evaluate operations, processes or products.
rationale: Performance evaluation against metrics is routinely dashboarded and can be narrated by models, but judging whether a process or product is acceptable involves contested standards and organisational stakes.

dwa_title: Review work orders or schedules to determine operations or procedures.
rationale: Work-order parsing and routing is well handled by MES/ERP rules and increasingly by document-reading models; the binding constraint is that the resulting operational decision is usually owned by a supervisor who reconciles the paperwork with shop-floor reality.

dwa_title: Analyze test results.
rationale: This is pure information processing over structured data, squarely in the sweet spot of statistical software and LLMs; the constraint is accountability for interpretation of anomalous or borderline results.

dwa_title: Evaluate energy production data.
rationale: Energy output data is already streamed into SCADA and analytics platforms that flag anomalies and compute performance metrics automatically; what remains human is deciding which deviations matter operationally and committing to a response.

dwa_title: Provide information to the general public.
rationale: Generic public information delivery is already displaced at scale by websites, chatbots and voice agents; only edge cases and vulnerable callers escalate to humans.

dwa_title: Correspond with customers to answer questions or resolve complaints.
rationale: Asynchronous written correspondence is the single most LLM-native customer task and is already automated at scale in email and ticketing systems.

dwa_title: Obtain property information.
rationale: Title, assessor and MLS records are digitised and API-accessible, so retrieval and summarisation are routine; only physical inspection or unrecorded encumbrances require a person.

dwa_title: Examine documents to verify adherence to requirements.
rationale: Document intake and rule-checking are well served by OCR plus LLM extraction, but requirement sets are idiosyncratic and edge-case calls still route to a named reviewer who accepts or rejects.

dwa_title: Interpret research or operational data.
rationale: Interpretation is pure symbolic reasoning over structured data, which frontier models handle well, but grounding conclusions in undocumented process context and owning the inference still requires the domain expert.

dwa_title: Process medical billing information.
rationale: Coding, claim scrubbing and adjudication are text-and-rules work highly suited to models, but payer-specific ambiguity and fraud/compliance liability keep a certified biller signing off.

dwa_title: Analyze data to inform operational decisions or activities.
rationale: BI and analytics pipelines plus LLM interpretation cover most of the analytic core; the binding constraint is that the decision context and consequences sit with an accountable manager.

dwa_title: Determine appropriate methods for data analysis.
rationale: Selecting statistical or modelling approaches is pure reasoning over data structure and question framing, which LLMs and AutoML do well; the constraint is that method choice encodes contestable assumptions a domain expert must defend.

dwa_title: Write grant proposals.
rationale: Grant text is prime LLM territory, yet the substantive scientific/programmatic claims and the institutional signature behind them must come from a responsible human.

dwa_title: Maintain records of sales or other business transactions.
rationale: POS, ERP and accounting platforms already capture and post transactions without human transcription; only exception handling and reconciliation of anomalies still pull a person in.

dwa_title: Provide basic information to guests, visitors, or clients.
rationale: Kiosks and digital concierges already substitute for much of this, though physical presence at a desk still carries a greeting and reassurance function machines handle poorly.

dwa_title: Provide recommendations to others about computer hardware.
rationale: Matching specifications and budget to hardware options is a structured comparison task already performed by configurators and recommendation systems; mistakes are cheap and reversible.

dwa_title: Perform student enrollment or registration activities.
rationale: Self-service student information systems already run enrollment end-to-end; humans persist mainly for exception handling and for applicants who need guidance.

dwa_title: Develop computer or online applications.
rationale: Greenfield application code is the single most automatable knowledge task today; what still fails is sustained autonomy over integration, ambiguous specs and production consequences.

dwa_title: Prepare proposal documents or grant applications.
rationale: Essentially a drafting-and-assembly task that current models handle at speed; human ownership persists for substantive claims and signature authority.

dwa_title: Communicate green energy production information.
rationale: This is largely reporting technical production data and explaining it, well within automated data-to-narrative pipelines; residual constraint is verification of figures that may carry regulatory or investor weight.

dwa_title: Refer customers to appropriate personnel.
rationale: Matching a stated need to the right internal party is a classification and routing problem already handled by deployed triage and ticketing systems.

dwa_title: Analyze financial information.
rationale: Purely symbolic work over structured and textual data that models handle well; the binding constraint is data trustworthiness and the fact that material financial conclusions are attested to by a named professional.

dwa_title: Develop database parameters or specifications.
rationale: Schema and parameter design is pure symbolic work well within model capability; the constraint is eliciting real business requirements and owning downstream performance and migration consequences.

dwa_title: Share sales-related or market information with colleagues.
rationale: CRM dashboards, automated pipeline digests and market-intelligence summarisation already push this information to colleagues without human mediation; only nuanced field colour still needs a person.

dwa_title: Communicate project information to others.
rationale: Status summarisation and distribution is already partly automated by project tooling and generative reporting; what resists is tailoring emphasis to audiences and fielding follow-up in real time.

dwa_title: Advise others on analytical techniques.
rationale: Explaining and recommending analytical methods is near-pure knowledge transfer that frontier models handle well; the binding constraint is that the advisee must trust and apply the method in a specific data context, which still routes through a credible human expert.

dwa_title: Analyze business or financial data.
rationale: BI pipelines plus LLM analysis can generate most descriptive and diagnostic findings; framing the business question and owning the interpretation for decision-makers is what still requires a human.

dwa_title: Prepare activity or work schedules.
rationale: Activity and work scheduling is a constrained optimization problem that deployed planning and project software solves routinely.

dwa_title: Advise patients on healthcare system processes.
rationale: Navigating referrals, coverage and paperwork is rule-based information retrieval that chatbots and payer portals already handle, though confused or distressed patients still need a human fallback.

dwa_title: Identify potential customers.
rationale: Prospect identification and lead scoring are already productised in CRM and intent-data platforms; errors are cheap and self-correcting, so little human anchoring is needed.

dwa_title: Prepare procedural documents.
rationale: Drafting SOPs and manuals is squarely in an LLM's wheelhouse, but the content must be sourced from subject-matter experts and formally approved, since people will follow the procedure as written.

dwa_title: Verify accuracy of data.
rationale: Automated reconciliation, checksum and validation-rule systems handle most accuracy checking already; the limit is verifying against ground truth that exists only outside the system.

dwa_title: Analyze quantitative data to determine effectiveness of treatments or therapies.
rationale: Statistical evaluation of treatment effectiveness is highly codified and tool-supported, but confounding, endpoint selection and regulatory sign-off keep a qualified analyst accountable.

dwa_title: Maintain knowledge of laws or regulations.
rationale: Regulatory horizon-scanning services already ingest and summarise rule changes automatically, but interpreting applicability to a specific operation and bearing compliance liability keeps a named professional in the loop.

dwa_title: Develop data analysis or data management procedures.
rationale: Analytic pipeline and methodology design is textual and code-like, squarely in LLM range, though validity of the analytic choices against messy real data still needs expert verification.

dwa_title: Prepare healthcare training materials.
rationale: Drafting is squarely in model capability, but clinical accuracy and accreditation of healthcare instruction demand review by a credentialed subject-matter expert who bears responsibility for errors taught to practitioners.

dwa_title: Research new technologies.
rationale: Technology scouting is almost pure reading and summarising over public information, the closest of this set to full automation; residual human value lies in filtering hype and relevance rather than in gathering.

dwa_title: Analyze traffic data.
rationale: Traffic counting, flow modelling and signal-timing optimisation run on deployed sensor and simulation platforms with minimal human input; engineering sign-off applies mainly when designs change infrastructure.

dwa_title: Order materials, supplies, or equipment.
rationale: Automatic replenishment and EDI purchase-order generation against catalogues and contracts are standard deployed practice; only exceptions, spend approval and new-supplier cases route to a human.

dwa_title: Conduct historical research.
rationale: The work is reading, collating and arguing over text, which models do well, but undigitised archives require physical access and source-credibility judgment plus hallucination risk keeps a historian accountable for the interpretation.

dwa_title: Monitor market conditions or trends.
rationale: Ingesting price, volume and news feeds and summarising trends is squarely a data-and-text task that deployed analytics plus LLMs already do continuously.

dwa_title: Prepare financial documents, reports, or budgets.
rationale: Ledger systems and LLMs can assemble and draft most statements and budget schedules, but attestation, assumption-setting and regulatory sign-off require a named accountable preparer.

dwa_title: Prepare proposals or grant applications to obtain project funding.
rationale: Writing and compliance-checking funding applications is text-heavy and well served by models, but budget commitments and certification of accuracy rest on a named applicant.

dwa_title: Gather organizational performance information.
rationale: Most performance data already flows through BI and ERP pipelines that automate collection; what resists is eliciting soft or undocumented performance signals from staff.

dwa_title: Design software applications.
rationale: Architectural design involves contested tradeoffs over cost, scale and maintainability elicited from stakeholders; models produce credible design options but cannot resolve which organisational constraints dominate.

dwa_title: Develop procedures for data management.
rationale: Drafting data governance, retention and access procedures is largely document generation an LLM handles well, but the procedures must bind to a specific organizational and regulatory context and be owned by a data steward.

dwa_title: Monitor financial information.
rationale: Financial data is already digital and structured, so continuous tracking, variance flagging and narrative summarisation are routine software functions; only the sign-off on what the numbers mean stays human.

dwa_title: Evaluate data quality.
rationale: Profiling, anomaly detection and rule-based data-quality tooling are mature, but deciding whether observed quality is fit for a given purpose remains a contextual professional judgment.

dwa_title: Monitor sales activities.
rationale: CRM and BI platforms already ingest pipeline data and generate alerts and forecasts end-to-end; the binding constraint is only whether anyone acts on the output.

dwa_title: Analyze data to identify or resolve operational problems.
rationale: Anomaly detection and root-cause suggestion are well automated, but confirming causes and enacting fixes usually requires tacit process knowledge and access to the physical or organisational system.

dwa_title: Verify accuracy of records.
rationale: Rule-based reconciliation, validation logic and OCR-plus-matching already handle routine record verification; humans are retained mainly for exception handling and attestation.

dwa_title: Document network-related activities or tasks.
rationale: Network discovery, configuration management and ticketing tools already auto-generate topology maps and activity logs, and LLMs write the narrative layer over them.

dwa_title: Provide educational information to the public.
rationale: The content is pure information transfer that models handle well, but public education often happens in live settings where reading an audience and adapting delivery still binds it to a person.

dwa_title: Order instructional or library materials or equipment.
rationale: The ordering transaction is trivially automatable, but selecting instructional and collection materials involves curricular fit, community standards and budget tradeoffs that a named selector typically owns.

dwa_title: Document design or development procedures.
rationale: Much of this can be synthesized from version control, issue trackers and design artifacts, but completeness and fidelity to what was actually done require human verification.

dwa_title: Present sustainable products or services information to the public.
rationale: This is essentially content generation and explanation, highly exposed to models; the constraint is that sustainability claims invite greenwashing liability and so need a human endorser.

dwa_title: Present information to the public.
rationale: Written and recorded public communication is already routinely machine-drafted, but live presentation and responsiveness to an audience still favour a human deliverer; the activity is too generic to score tightly.

dwa_title: Document operational procedures.
rationale: Writing up how a process works is near-pure text generation that LLMs handle well, but the tacit, undocumented knowledge of the actual procedure has to be elicited from practitioners and validated before it becomes an authoritative document.

dwa_title: Report information to managers or other personnel.
rationale: Routine status and exception reporting upward is largely a data-aggregation-and-summarise task already handled by dashboards and automated reports.

dwa_title: Review documents or materials for compliance with policies or regulations.
rationale: Regulatory interpretation is textual and highly LLM-exposed, but ambiguity in how rules apply to a specific document plus the liability attached to a compliance determination keeps a human as the decision owner.

dwa_title: Enter codes or other information into computers.
rationale: OCR, document AI and RPA handle structured keying at scale in production today; residual human work is exception queues and ambiguous source documents.

dwa_title: Enter patient or treatment data into computers.
rationale: Ambient scribes and interface engines already draft and post clinical data, but a licensed clinician must attest to the record because coding and charting errors propagate into care decisions and billing liability.

dwa_title: Analyze impact of legal or regulatory changes.
rationale: Tracking and summarising legal change is largely text analysis, but forecasting how a change will bite on a specific organisation involves ambiguity and enforcement-practice knowledge that models get wrong in ways only counsel can catch.

dwa_title: Research crop management methods.
rationale: Agronomic literature and trial-data analysis are highly LLM-exposed; field plot experimentation and site-specific verification remain physical and seasonal.

dwa_title: Verify information or specifications.
rationale: Cross-checking stated values against authoritative sources is highly rule-based and well served by validation software and LLM extraction, but the binding constraint is access to trustworthy reference sources and the residual need for a human to sign off on discrepancies.

dwa_title: Analyze costs and benefits of proposed designs or projects.
rationale: The arithmetic of cost-benefit analysis is trivially automatable, but the results hinge on assumptions, discount rates and scope choices that are contestable and must be owned by a human analyst.

dwa_title: Develop technical or scientific databases.
rationale: Model-generated DDL and ingestion code is already practical, but domain-specific data semantics, provenance and curation decisions still require a scientist's involvement.

dwa_title: Develop specifications or procedures for website development or maintenance.
rationale: Web standards, style guides and maintenance procedures are text artifacts LLMs produce well; the constraint is eliciting and arbitrating what the organisation actually wants and enforcing it.

dwa_title: Develop information communication procedures.
rationale: Communication protocols are essentially documentation work that models draft well; the constraint is fitting them to an organization's actual channels, culture and compliance context, which requires internal knowledge and sign-off.

dwa_title: Prepare detailed work plans.
rationale: The output is a structured document, squarely within LLM capability; what stops full automation is dependence on undocumented site and resource realities and the need for a manager to own the plan.

dwa_title: Write reports or evaluations.
rationale: Drafting is heavily exposed, but 'evaluations' often carry consequences for people or programs, so the evaluative judgment and its attribution must remain with a named human.

dwa_title: Gather customer or product information to determine customer needs.
rationale: Behavioural analytics, product catalogues and conversational agents already infer customer needs end-to-end in commercial deployment; errors are cheap and instantly correctable.

dwa_title: Evaluate utility of software or hardware technologies.
rationale: Comparing specs, benchmarks and fit-to-requirement is nearly pure information work well within model reach; what blocks full automation is procurement accountability and tacit knowledge of the local environment.

dwa_title: Analyze environmental regulations to ensure organizational compliance.
rationale: Mapping regulatory text onto operational facts is exactly what language models do well, yet compliance determinations carry legal liability that requires a named accountable officer to certify.

dwa_title: Prepare sales or other contracts.
rationale: Template-and-clause assembly is already largely software-driven and LLMs draft terms well, but the binding constraint is that a named party or licensed agent must own the enforceable commitments and negotiated deviations.

dwa_title: Prepare contracts, disclosures, or applications.
rationale: Drafting contracts, disclosures and applications is text generation over structured facts, which frontier models handle; disclosure obligations carry legal liability that requires a responsible human signatory.

dwa_title: Inform viewers, listeners, or audiences.
rationale: Automated scripting, voice synthesis and synthetic presenters already deliver informational broadcasts, but editorial responsibility and audience trust in a recognisable human still gate full substitution.

dwa_title: Analyze market conditions or trends.
rationale: Gathering, summarising and comparing market evidence is squarely in frontier-model territory; the constraint is proprietary or tacit channel knowledge and the strategic weighting of ambiguous signals.

dwa_title: Document technical design details.
rationale: Design documentation can be largely generated from CAD models, code and change logs, but accurately capturing design intent and rationale still requires the designer's own account.

dwa_title: Prepare research or technical reports on environmental issues.
rationale: Environmental impact and compliance documents follow templates an LLM handles well, but they are regulatory filings typically requiring a licensed professional's certification of field data and conclusions.

dwa_title: Research livestock management methods.
rationale: Synthesising published husbandry evidence is squarely in model territory, but validating methods against live herds and local conditions needs hands-on trial work.

dwa_title: Communicate organizational information to customers or other stakeholders.
rationale: Routine stakeholder and customer communication is already heavily automated through templated messaging, CRM workflows and conversational agents; only sensitive or relationship-critical disclosures are held back.

dwa_title: Prepare documentation for permits or licenses.
rationale: Permit and licence packages are highly structured and form-driven, so extraction and population are automatable; the constraint is jurisdiction-specific evidentiary requirements and the signed attestation of accuracy demanded by the issuing authority.

dwa_title: Research sustainable agricultural processes or practices.
rationale: Sustainability research is information-synthesis heavy, but weighing contested trade-offs across yield, soil and emissions is a judgment call requiring empirical field validation.

dwa_title: Prepare drawings or diagrams of products or services.
rationale: Generative image and diagramming tools already produce usable illustrative drawings from specifications; the remaining constraint is fidelity to client intent and technical accuracy checking rather than accountability.

dwa_title: Schedule activities or facility use.
rationale: Generic facility and activity booking is a solved calendaring and resource-allocation problem with mature commercial software; only contested priority calls need a person.

dwa_title: Develop models of information or communications systems.
rationale: Wholly digital, documentation-like work over formal notations where frontier models are strong; what stops full automation is eliciting real requirements and validating the model against messy existing infrastructure.

dwa_title: Communicate results of environmental research.
rationale: Drafting reports, visualisations and summaries of environmental findings is squarely in LLM territory, but the scientist must vouch for the interpretation and defend it to regulators or the public.

dwa_title: Perform clerical work in medical settings.
rationale: Scheduling, records and transcription are automatable, but medical front-office work bundles in-person patient handling and physical chart/specimen logistics that keep a person on site.

dwa_title: Compile environmental or climatological data.
rationale: Environmental and climate data flows are already collected by automated sensor networks and ingested into standard archives; human effort persists mainly in instrument maintenance and QC of legacy records.

dwa_title: Resolve computer software problems.
rationale: Patch lookup, config repair and code-level debugging are text-native tasks with strong model performance, but authority to change production software and verify the result keeps a human in the loop.

dwa_title: Perform marketing activities.
rationale: Copy, segmentation, campaign optimisation and analytics are already substantially machine-run; strategic positioning and brand accountability keep humans in the loop.

dwa_title: Evaluate reports or designs to determine work needs.
rationale: Reading a report or design and inferring what work is needed is squarely in LLM territory, but the inference drives resource commitments and rests on tacit context the documents omit.

dwa_title: Conduct research to gain information about products or processes.
rationale: Written at high generality: the information-gathering core is retrieval and synthesis that tools already handle, while any empirical testing component pulls it back into the physical world.

dwa_title: Monitor external affairs or events affecting business operations.
rationale: Scanning regulatory, political and competitive signals is text-native, but deciding which weak signals actually threaten the business relies on insider context and executive judgment.

dwa_title: Design computer modeling or simulation programs.
rationale: The binding constraint is validation: models write simulation code fluently but cannot certify that the abstraction faithfully represents the modelled physical or economic system.

dwa_title: Explain regulations, policies, or procedures.
rationale: Interpreting and restating rules in plain language is a core LLM strength, but authoritative interpretation of regulation carries legal consequence that organizations still route through accountable staff.

dwa_title: Prepare staff schedules or work assignments.
rationale: Workforce-management software already generates compliant rosters from demand forecasts, skills and availability; human input mainly handles fairness complaints and last-minute exceptions.

dwa_title: Test software performance.
rationale: Load, profiling and regression testing are already scripted into CI/CD pipelines and the interpretation of results is text-and-metric reasoning that models handle well; the binding constraint is only deciding which performance targets matter.

dwa_title: Model operational processes.
rationale: Code generation and simulation tooling can build and calibrate process models quickly, but choosing the abstraction, boundary conditions and validation criteria is a contested modelling judgment that no deployed system owns.

dwa_title: Prepare reports summarizing patient diagnostic or care activities.
rationale: Summarising diagnostic and care data is exactly what clinical-note LLM tools already do well; the binding constraint is clinician sign-off and liability for diagnostic content.

dwa_title: Analyze design requirements for computer or electronics systems.
rationale: Requirements are textual and highly LLM-tractable, but they arrive incomplete and contradictory from stakeholders, so eliciting and reconciling intent remains the bottleneck.

dwa_title: Develop computer or information systems.
rationale: Coding agents now generate and integrate substantial system components, but eliciting requirements from stakeholders and owning architectural trade-offs across a live organisation still requires a human to hold the thread.

dwa_title: Coordinate reporting or editing activities.
rationale: Drafting, assignment triage and copy review are squarely in model capability, yet editorial accountability for what is published and the handling of writers stays with a named editor.

dwa_title: Assess database performance.
rationale: Query telemetry, APM dashboards and automatic index/plan advisors already measure and diagnose database performance end-to-end; the binding constraint is acting on findings in production, not detecting them.

dwa_title: Evaluate applicable laws and regulations to determine impact on organizational activities.
rationale: The binding constraint is professional responsibility: legal applicability opinions must be attributable to a licensed or officer-level human even when the analytic draft is machine-produced.

dwa_title: Develop detailed project plans.
rationale: Project plans are text plus dependency logic that models and PM software generate well; the constraint is negotiating scope and resources with stakeholders and accountability for schedule and budget commitments.

dwa_title: Document operational activities.
rationale: Operational logging is increasingly captured automatically by instrumented systems; residual human input is needed only where events are observed off-system.

dwa_title: Recommend changes to improve computer or information systems.
rationale: Analysing system performance and drafting improvement proposals is strongly model-exposed; what blocks full automation is access to organisational constraints and the need for someone accountable when a recommended change breaks production.

dwa_title: Classify organisms based on their characteristics or behavior.
rationale: Image classifiers, acoustic ID and DNA barcoding pipelines already assign taxa routinely and at scale; the residue is novel or cryptic taxa where formal taxonomic judgment and specimen handling still require a systematist.

dwa_title: Develop scientific or mathematical models.
rationale: This is essentially symbolic and computational reasoning where LLMs plus solvers are strongest; validation against reality and assumption selection remain the human-held step.

dwa_title: Prepare information or documentation related to legal or regulatory matters.
rationale: Legal and regulatory drafting is the paradigm case of high LLM leverage, yet unauthorised-practice rules, filing certifications and liability for misstatement anchor responsibility to a licensed human.

dwa_title: Explain technical product or service information to customers.
rationale: Retrieval-grounded assistants are already commercially deployed for exactly this explaining-to-customers function; the residual human need is escalation for frustrated customers and high-stakes specification claims.

dwa_title: Research engineering applications of emerging technologies.
rationale: This is largely desk-based scanning and synthesis of technical literature and vendor data, which frontier models do well; what they cannot own is the engineer's discriminating judgement about which emerging technology is actually viable for a given context.

dwa_title: Analyze environmental data.
rationale: The statistical pipeline from sensor or monitoring data to trend detection is highly automatable, but regulatory environmental conclusions must be defensible and signed by a qualified professional, keeping a human in the loop on interpretation.

dwa_title: Troubleshoot issues with computer applications or systems.
rationale: Diagnosis from logs, error strings and user descriptions is squarely in frontier-model range, and AI support agents already close simple tickets; the limit is eliciting accurate information from users and safely executing fixes in live systems.

dwa_title: Assess the cost effectiveness of products, projects, or services.
rationale: Cost-benefit modelling is quantitative and tool-supported, so models do the analysis readily; the constraint is choosing assumptions and defending them to decision-makers.

dwa_title: Identify information technology project resource requirements.
rationale: Almost entirely document- and data-based reasoning that models do strongly, but accurate IT resourcing depends on undocumented organizational context, stakeholder negotiation and commitments that a named project owner must make.

dwa_title: Collect data about customer needs.
rationale: Automated surveys, review mining and conversational agents already harvest stated needs at scale; the binding constraint is eliciting unstated or latent needs through rapport-based interviewing, where a human interlocutor still gets richer signal.

dwa_title: Develop software or applications for scientific or technical use.
rationale: Scientific software is textual and highly LLM-exposed, but correctness must be anchored to domain theory and experimental ground truth that only the responsible researcher can attest to.

dwa_title: Develop guidelines for system implementation.
rationale: Implementation guidance is structured technical writing over known architectures, which models handle well; the binding limit is unwritten knowledge of the target environment and stakeholder buy-in.

dwa_title: Document test results.
rationale: Automated test harnesses and LIMS already capture and report results without human transcription; the constraint is regulated contexts (clinical, aerospace, certified labs) where a qualified individual must sign off on the record's validity.

dwa_title: Compile geographic or related data.
rationale: Remote sensing, GPS feeds and automated GIS ingestion dominate geographic data compilation; field survey and ground-truthing remain the embodied residual.

dwa_title: Analyze test or validation data.
rationale: Pass/fail checking against defined acceptance criteria is already automated in test benches and validation suites; the residual human role is adjudicating out-of-spec and ambiguous cases and attesting to validation.

dwa_title: Document technical specifications or requirements.
rationale: Specification writing is text-heavy and heavily LLM-assisted, but requirements must be elicited and negotiated among stakeholders and then owned contractually by a responsible engineer.

dwa_title: Send information, materials or documentation.
rationale: Electronic distribution is trivially automated and workflow systems handle routing; only the physical packaging/posting fraction still needs hands.

dwa_title: Estimate costs or terms of sales.
rationale: CPQ and dynamic pricing engines already generate quotes and terms automatically for standardised offerings; bespoke deals hinge on reading the customer and on commitment authority a human holds.

dwa_title: Inform the public about policies, services or procedures.
rationale: Public information delivery is largely text/voice generation over a known policy corpus, which chatbots already do at scale; the binding constraint is institutional liability for misinformation and the need for a named spokesperson in contested cases.

dwa_title: Provide information to coworkers.
rationale: Answering colleagues' informational questions is retrieval and explanation, which internal knowledge assistants already do at scale.

dwa_title: Prepare project budgets.
rationale: Cost estimating is structured numeric modeling well suited to models and templates; the binding constraint is that assumptions must be owned and defended by an accountable budget holder.

dwa_title: Analyze project data to determine specifications or requirements.
rationale: Deriving specifications from project data is a synthesis task models handle well on clean inputs; the constraint is that much of the governing context is unwritten and must be negotiated with clients and teams.

dwa_title: Analyze health-related data.
rationale: Health data analysis is largely information processing that models and analytics tools handle well, but clinical and regulatory governance requires a licensed human to own conclusions drawn from patient data.

dwa_title: Estimate demand for products or services.
rationale: Automated demand-forecasting engines run unattended in retail and supply chain, yet structural breaks, promotions and new products require human override because the historical series stops being informative.

dwa_title: Prepare official health documents or records.
rationale: Generation of official health records is textual and highly LLM-exposed, but statutory and licensure rules require a credentialed human to attest to the contents.

dwa_title: Maintain medical facility records.
rationale: EHR and health-information-management systems automate storage, indexing and coding suggestions, but privacy law and release-of-information rules require a named custodian answerable for record integrity.

dwa_title: Evaluate student work.
rationale: Automated essay and code scoring is deployed and accurate on average, but grades are consequential records that an instructor must own, and formative feedback depends on knowing the student.

dwa_title: Apply information technology to solve business or other applied problems.
rationale: Translating a messy business problem into a technical solution is heavily LLM-assisted in analysis and prototyping, but the binding constraint is diagnosing the real organisational problem with stakeholders who state it imprecisely.

dwa_title: Develop proposals for current or prospective customers.
rationale: Drafting is near-fully LLM-exposed, but pricing, commitments and reading the customer's unstated priorities require a human owning the client relationship.

dwa_title: Take product orders from customers.
rationale: Online ordering portals and deployed voice-AI order takers handle standard order capture reliably; the constraint is only upsell rapport and messy or atypical customer requests.

dwa_title: Develop performance metrics or standards related to information technology.
rationale: Drafting SLAs, KPIs and IT standards is document work models handle well, but choosing targets that people will be measured against requires negotiation and managerial ownership.

dwa_title: Maintain medical or professional knowledge.
rationale: Literature surveillance, summarisation and guideline tracking are strongly LLM-exposed, but the binding constraint is that the competence must reside in the licensed clinician who will act on it and be answerable for outdated practice.

dwa_title: Schedule instructional activities.
rationale: Timetabling engines already solve room, instructor and cohort constraints; the friction is negotiating instructor preferences and pedagogical sequencing, which is small relative to the combinatorial core.

dwa_title: Explain financial information to customers.
rationale: Explanation of statements, products and terms is readily generated, but financial suitability and disclosure rules bind a licensed individual to what the customer is told.

dwa_title: Communicate health and wellness information to the public.
rationale: Health messaging is text and media production that models do well, but public health claims require an accountable clinician or agency to vouch for accuracy given the harm from misinformation.

dwa_title: Provide technical information or assistance to public.
rationale: Technical Q&A is squarely in LLM territory and already deployed as support assistants; the constraint is that technical advice to outsiders can carry liability and often needs site- or case-specific verification.

dwa_title: Order medical supplies or equipment.
rationale: Par-level replenishment from clinical supply systems is already largely automatic; the residual human role is handling shortages, substitutions and regulated or controlled items.

dwa_title: Maintain medical records.
rationale: Most maintenance operations are database transactions machines handle well; the constraint is regulated accountability for completeness, amendment and disclosure of the legal medical record.

dwa_title: Maintain regulatory or compliance documentation.
rationale: Document control, versioning and retention are classic workflow-automation targets, but deciding what satisfies an inspector or auditor and certifying the record remains a named compliance officer's duty.

dwa_title: Develop mathematical models of environmental conditions.
rationale: Model fitting, calibration and code generation are heavily tooled and partly automated already; the residual human role is choosing structural assumptions and defending predictions used in regulation or risk decisions.

dwa_title: Document design or operational test results.
rationale: Test benches and instrumentation already auto-log data, and language models can draft the narrative and interpretation, but the binding constraint is authenticated engineering sign-off on what the results mean for a design's fitness.

dwa_title: Conduct quantitative failure analyses of operational data.
rationale: Reliability statistics (Weibull fits, Pareto/root-cause ranking) are well-codified and scriptable, but linking statistical signal to true physical failure mechanisms needs engineering knowledge of the asset and carries safety accountability.

dwa_title: Estimate time requirements for development or production projects.
rationale: Historical-data-driven schedule estimation is well suited to algorithms and already embedded in project tools, yet novel scope, dependency risk and organisational optimism require human calibration and commitment.

dwa_title: Prepare operational budgets.
rationale: Rolling forecasts and variance-driven budget builds are already semi-automated in FP&A software; the allocation choices and their defense before leadership remain a human responsibility.

dwa_title: Evaluate scholarly materials.
rationale: Reading and critiquing scholarly text is squarely in an LLM's wheelhouse, but originality and significance judgements are contested and scholarly norms require a named, reputationally accountable reviewer.

dwa_title: Prepare maps.
rationale: GIS pipelines already auto-generate styled cartography from spatial databases; the binding constraint is source-data validation and cartographic design choices for a particular audience, which still needs a human editor.

dwa_title: Identify sustainable business practices.
rationale: Largely a research-and-synthesis task over standards, supply-chain data and best practice, which models do well; applicability to a specific operation and reporting credibility keep a human in charge.

dwa_title: Instruct staff in work policies or procedures.
rationale: Policy and procedure content is fully codified text, so generation, delivery and comprehension checks are readily automated; what remains is answering edge-case questions and confirming that staff actually acknowledged and understood the rules.

dwa_title: Research energy production, use, or conservation.
rationale: Energy data are abundant and machine-readable, making modelling and literature review highly automatable; the sticking point is choosing scenario assumptions and reconciling field measurements with models.

dwa_title: Identify new applications for existing technologies.
rationale: Analogical search across technology and market literature is a strong LLM capability, but validating commercial viability requires tacit domain knowledge and contested strategic judgment.

dwa_title: Analyze Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data for use in green applications.
rationale: Standard GIS overlay, suitability and siting analyses are scriptable and increasingly agent-driven; what resists is choosing weighting criteria and defending siting tradeoffs to stakeholders.

dwa_title: Load digital images onto computers or websites.
rationale: Ingest, tag and publish pipelines with automated metadata and CMS APIs already do this end-to-end; only aesthetic selection or rights checking calls for a person.

dwa_title: Schedule patient procedures or appointments.
rationale: Patient self-scheduling is widely deployed, but procedure booking involves clinical prerequisites, prep instructions and urgency triage where a misordered slot carries real patient harm, so oversight persists.

dwa_title: Provide customer service to clients or users.
rationale: Tier-one service is being absorbed by deployed AI agents, but emotional escalation, goodwill concessions and exception handling still get handed to a human with authority to act.

dwa_title: Maintain records, documents, or other files.
rationale: Document management systems with automated classification and retention rules already handle this; physical paper files and scanning are the remaining manual residue.

dwa_title: Estimate operational costs.
rationale: Operational cost modelling runs on structured historical data that software already aggregates well; what resists is the forward-looking assumption setting about utilisation, inflation and vendor behaviour.

dwa_title: Analyze physical, survey, or geographic data.
rationale: Survey adjustment and spatial data reduction are already software-driven, but blunder detection and legally certified boundary or engineering conclusions still attach to a licensed human.

dwa_title: Develop specifications for computer network operation.
rationale: Network design specification is well-covered by documented patterns and vendor tooling that models reproduce fluently, but capacity, security and continuity risk keep an accountable architect in the loop.

dwa_title: Prepare reports detailing student activities or performance.
rationale: Grade and attendance data already auto-populate report cards, but the qualitative narrative rests on a teacher's direct observation of a child and is read by parents as a professional judgment.

dwa_title: Analyze data to determine project feasibility.
rationale: The modelling and sensitivity analysis are automatable, but the assumptions driving a feasibility verdict are contestable and carry investment consequences someone must stand behind.

dwa_title: Analyze geological or geographical data.
rationale: Subsurface and spatial datasets are ambiguous and underdetermined, so models accelerate processing and hypothesis generation while the binding constraint remains expert reconciliation of conflicting geological interpretations.

dwa_title: Conduct research on social issues.
rationale: Secondary data analysis and literature synthesis are highly exposed, but primary collection from human subjects involves consent, trust and ethics oversight, and causal claims about society remain contested expert judgment.

dwa_title: Research design or application of green technologies.
rationale: Green-technology assessment is document- and data-heavy and thus well within model reach, but site-specific feasibility and lifecycle assumptions remain contested calls a human must select and defend.

dwa_title: Plan menu options.
rationale: Menu planning is largely constraint optimisation over cost, seasonality and demand data that software handles well, but final selection depends on tasted quality and local clientele knowledge.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of structures or landscapes.
rationale: Rendering engines and diffusion models produce convincing structure and landscape visuals cheaply, but fidelity to the actual designed geometry and site conditions requires a human driving the model.

dwa_title: Communicate with the public on environmental issues.
rationale: Material preparation and routine inquiry response are highly model-exposed, but public environmental communication is politically contested and often occurs in hearings and site meetings where a credible human must stand behind claims.

dwa_title: Conduct climatological research.
rationale: The work is almost entirely computational over large archived datasets, so the constraint is not embodiment but the contested design of models and attribution claims that a scientist must defend.

dwa_title: Advise others on logistics topics.
rationale: Routing, regulatory and carrier-selection questions are highly structured and already served by optimisation software plus model-based guidance; disruption handling and negotiated exceptions keep a human in the loop.

dwa_title: Create maps.
rationale: Automated map compilation from geospatial layers is routine, yet decisions about projection, generalisation and what to omit carry interpretive weight a human still owns.

dwa_title: Market products, services, or events.
rationale: Content generation, targeting and campaign optimisation are already machine-run in ad platforms, but positioning strategy, brand risk and channel choice still hinge on human market judgement and sign-off.

dwa_title: Coordinate with external parties to exchange information.
rationale: Routine information exchange is largely message composition and routing, already partly handled by EDI/portals and well suited to LLMs, but deciding what may be disclosed to whom still needs a responsible human.

dwa_title: Design healthcare-related software applications.
rationale: Same design reasoning as general software but bound by HIPAA, safety-critical validation and device regulation, which require a named human to attest to design controls.

dwa_title: Identify opportunities for green initiatives.
rationale: Scanning regulations, benchmarks and operational data to propose sustainability options is well within LLM reach, but selecting initiatives depends on organisational context and stakeholder buy-in that a model cannot own.

dwa_title: Analyze laboratory findings.
rationale: Once findings are digital, correlation and flagging are well within model reach, but clinical or scientific interpretation that drives consequential decisions needs a credentialed signer.

dwa_title: Analyze test or performance data to assess equipment operation.
rationale: Condition-monitoring and predictive-maintenance platforms already flag equipment degradation from sensor streams with little human input; interpretation becomes human only when the recommended action is costly or safety-critical.

dwa_title: Maintain operational records.
rationale: Where operations are already digitally instrumented, record maintenance is a solved software problem; the residual human work is capturing events that never touch a system.

dwa_title: Create schematic drawings for electronics.
rationale: EDA tools already automate symbol placement, netlist checks and routing, and models can draft circuit topologies from specs, but binding constraint is that correct component selection and manufacturability still require an engineer to verify and sign off before fabrication.

dwa_title: Develop methods of social or economic research.
rationale: Survey instruments, sampling frames and identification strategies are pure information work that frontier models handle well; the constraint is contested methodological judgment that peers must be able to challenge and a researcher must defend.

dwa_title: Develop testing routines or procedures.
rationale: Test-case generation from specifications is one of the strongest current LLM applications, but coverage adequacy for safety-relevant systems and physical test rig setup keep a human owner.

dwa_title: Maintain operational records or records systems.
rationale: Modern ERP, MES and logging systems already capture and organize operational records automatically; the binding constraint is data entry at points where events are not yet instrumented and exception handling when entries conflict.

dwa_title: Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency.
rationale: Process-mining and analytics tools plus LLM reasoning surface inefficiencies readily, but diagnosing real causes usually requires on-site observation and negotiation with the people doing the work.

dwa_title: Analyze green technology design requirements.
rationale: Standards, incentives and lifecycle data are documentary and machine-readable, but green criteria are contested and rapidly shifting, so defensible interpretation still rests with a human specialist.

dwa_title: Estimate technical or resource requirements for development or production projects.
rationale: Parametric estimating software plus models can generate resource takeoffs quickly, but the binding constraint is unmodelled project-specific scope uncertainty that an estimator must judge and stand behind in a bid.

dwa_title: Select educational materials or equipment.
rationale: Content matching to standards and learner level is strongly model-exposed, but adoption decisions carry pedagogical judgment about specific students and are subject to district or parental accountability.

dwa_title: Provide technical support for computer network issues.
rationale: Automated monitoring and scripted remediation cover routine faults, but the binding constraint is that many network problems terminate in cabling, hardware or on-site device access.

dwa_title: Configure computer networks.
rationale: Infrastructure-as-code, zero-touch provisioning and SDN controllers already push configurations automatically, but design choices, security posture and change approval still route through a named engineer because a bad push can black out a site.

dwa_title: Develop procedures to evaluate organizational activities.
rationale: Evaluation frameworks and metrics can be drafted by a model, but choosing what counts as organizational success is politically negotiated and must be owned by management.

dwa_title: Appraise environmental impact of regulations or policies.
rationale: The evidence base is documentary and highly amenable to model synthesis, but environmental impact appraisal rests on contested causal and valuation assumptions that expert reviewers and statutory processes must adjudicate.

dwa_title: Develop theories or models of social phenomena.
rationale: Social theorising is pure discursive reasoning and hence maximally LLM-exposed, but contestability of interpretation and the need for scholarly ownership of claims keep a human at the centre.

dwa_title: Create diagrams or blueprints for workpieces or products.
rationale: CAD automation and model-based definition can generate dimensioned drawings from parametric models, but tolerance decisions and manufacturability sign-off still attach to a drafter or engineer because errors propagate into scrapped parts.

dwa_title: Develop organizational methods or procedures.
rationale: Procedure and method design is largely document work that LLMs draft competently, but fitting it to tacit local workflow realities and signing off on compliance keeps a human owner.

dwa_title: Teach others to use computer equipment or hardware.
rationale: Explanatory content and troubleshooting dialogue are well within current models, but showing someone physically how to handle, connect or service hardware still benefits from co-presence.

dwa_title: Arrange delivery of goods or services.
rationale: Logistics and dispatch platforms already book, route and confirm deliveries end-to-end; only exception handling and negotiation with counterparties still pulls in a human.

dwa_title: Collect archival data.
rationale: Binding constraint is that much archival material is physical, uncatalogued or idiosyncratically stored, requiring on-site handling and provenance judgement before any machine reading can occur.

dwa_title: Determine types of equipment, tools, or materials needed for jobs.
rationale: Specifying equipment and materials is codified knowledge work that estimating software and LLMs handle well from specs, but binding constraint is tacit site/job knowledge and the fact that a wrong bill of materials creates real downstream cost, so a qualified human signs off.

dwa_title: Draw detailed or technical illustrations.
rationale: Generative imaging cannot hold dimensional and part-level precision, so technical illustration still runs through human-driven CAD/vector work; models mainly accelerate layout, callouts and variants.

dwa_title: Schedule medical facility use.
rationale: Room, theatre and equipment booking is a constrained optimisation already handled by deployed hospital scheduling systems; the residual human role is exception handling when clinical urgency overrides the algorithm.

dwa_title: Estimate costs for projects or productions.
rationale: Digital takeoff and parametric estimating tools automate the quantity and unit-rate mechanics, but scope interpretation from incomplete drawings or scripts, and ownership of the committed number, stay human.

dwa_title: Develop marketing plans or strategies.
rationale: Models draft credible strategy from data, but committing budget requires reading internal politics and betting on contested assumptions about competitor and consumer response.

dwa_title: Exchange information with colleagues.
rationale: Bidirectional exchange presupposes two informed participants with context and stake; automation handles the transmission and summarisation layer only.

dwa_title: Advise patients on preventive care techniques.
rationale: Preventive-care content is protocolised and well within model capability; the constraint is licensure for patient-facing counselling and the behaviour-change relationship that drives adherence.

dwa_title: Develop computer or information security policies or procedures.
rationale: Mapping controls to frameworks and drafting policy language is near-ideal LLM work, but an accountable officer must ratify risk acceptance and attest to compliance for audit and liability purposes.

dwa_title: Collaborate with others to develop or implement marketing strategies.
rationale: Strategy generation, segmentation analysis and campaign drafting are squarely in model territory; the binding constraint is that stakeholder buy-in and internal negotiation over resources happen between people.

dwa_title: Conduct scientific research of organizational behavior or processes.
rationale: Design, analysis and write-up are heavily machine-assisted, but human-subject data collection and research-ethics responsibility keep a named investigator in the loop.

dwa_title: Verify customer credit information.
rationale: Credit bureau APIs and automated decisioning engines already perform this end-to-end at scale; remaining human involvement is mostly exception handling and regulatory adverse-action justification.

dwa_title: Develop educational or training programs.
rationale: Needs analysis and content build-out are highly text-based and already tooled, yet stakeholder alignment on what the training must achieve and compliance sign-off keep a human in the lead.

dwa_title: Promote products, services, or programs.
rationale: Promotional content production and distribution are highly LLM-exposed; the residual human work is relationship-based outreach and reputational risk ownership.

dwa_title: Advise others on the development or use of new technologies.
rationale: Advising on emerging technology means forecasting under genuine uncertainty and convincing decision-makers to commit resources, so the model supplies synthesis while a human owns the bet.

dwa_title: Evaluate new technologies or methods.
rationale: Literature synthesis and comparative appraisal are core model strengths, but credible evaluation usually requires hands-on trialling and contextual fit judgment.

dwa_title: Evaluate the characteristics of green technologies.
rationale: Most of the work is synthesising specifications, lifecycle data and standards, which a model does well, but credible assessment still depends on field/test data and contested sustainability criteria that a human must select and defend.

dwa_title: Interpret design or operational test results.
rationale: Models can compute against spec limits and draft interpretations, but deciding whether anomalous results mean a design flaw, a test artifact or an acceptable deviation is contested engineering judgment that must be signed off.

dwa_title: Plan social sciences research.
rationale: Instrument design, sampling frames and analysis plans are almost purely textual and statistical, so LLM leverage is high; human-subjects ethics review requires a named principal investigator.

dwa_title: Research advanced engineering designs or applications.
rationale: Advanced design research is analytic and simulation-driven, so models and solvers cover much of it; the constraint is novelty — frontier design questions have no precedent in training data and require verified experimental or computational validation.
