dwa_title: Estimate supplies, ingredients, or staff requirements for food preparation activities.
rationale: Demand forecasting and par-level software already computes ingredient and labor needs from POS history; the residual human role is correcting for local events, deliveries and on-hand stock that the system cannot observe.

dwa_title: Advise others on green energy or related technologies.
rationale: Technology comparison, incentive rules and sizing calculations are highly tractable for models; the constraint is site-specific data capture and the fact that a named engineer or consultant typically stands behind a recommendation involving capital expenditure.

dwa_title: Test computer system operations to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Continuous monitoring, synthetic transactions and automated regression/test pipelines are standard practice; the remaining human role is triaging ambiguous failures and owning production go/no-go calls.

dwa_title: Forecast economic, political, or social trends.
rationale: Models can synthesise vast evidence and articulate scenarios, but the activity is irreducibly contested prediction where accuracy is unverifiable in advance and institutions want a named forecaster to defend the call.

dwa_title: Develop theories or models of physical phenomena.
rationale: Frontier models manipulate formalism and derive consequences competently, but genuinely novel theory construction still depends on human taste about which abstraction is worth pursuing and on empirical confrontation.

dwa_title: Analyze test data or images to inform diagnosis or treatment.
rationale: FDA-cleared imaging and lab-interpretation AI is deployed but almost universally as a flagging or triage aid; a radiologist or pathologist must sign the diagnostic report.

dwa_title: Develop educational programs.
rationale: Curriculum architecture, sequencing and materials are strongly model-assisted, but fitting a program to institutional constraints, accreditation and real learner populations requires a human owner.

dwa_title: Maintain computer networks to enhance performance and user access.
rationale: Configuration, monitoring, tuning and troubleshooting are software-mediated and highly model-exposed, but change control on production networks keeps a human owning the risk, plus residual cabling work.

dwa_title: Tutor students who need extra assistance.
rationale: AI tutors already deliver competent one-to-one explanation and practice; the binding constraint is sustaining motivation and diagnosing affective barriers in struggling learners.

dwa_title: Analyze security of systems, network, or data.
rationale: Scanners, SIEM correlation and increasingly LLM triage automate detection breadth, but adversarial novelty, false-positive arbitration and risk acceptance decisions keep a named security owner in the loop.

dwa_title: Assess product or process usefulness.
rationale: Usefulness is defined relative to user needs and organisational goals that are elicited from people and weighed subjectively; models can structure and argue the case but cannot own the value judgement.

dwa_title: Purchase materials, equipment, or other resources.
rationale: Sourcing, comparison and requisition drafting are highly model-exposed, but committing organisational funds involves supplier negotiation and a delegated signing authority that must rest with a person.

dwa_title: Estimate time or monetary resources needed to complete projects.
rationale: Models can assemble takeoffs, historical analogues and schedules quickly, but the binding constraint is contested assumptions about scope, productivity and risk that a named estimator must own when the bid is committed.

dwa_title: Maintain records of customer accounts.
rationale: CRM and billing platforms maintain account records automatically from transactions; exceptions and disputes are the only part needing human handling.

dwa_title: Review environmental permits, plans, or reports.
rationale: Permit and report review is document-based and highly assistable, but the determination is a regulatory act that typically requires a licensed or delegated official to sign and defend.

dwa_title: Evaluate potential of products, technologies, or resources.
rationale: Forecasting potential rests on contested assumptions about future markets and capabilities where evidence is thin, so models can scaffold the case but cannot settle it.

dwa_title: Review details of technical drawings or specifications.
rationale: CAD/PDM software already extracts dimensions and tolerances automatically, but multimodal reading of legacy or annotated drawings remains error-prone and misread specifications propagate into costly physical rework.

dwa_title: Research environmental impact of industrial or development activities.
rationale: Literature synthesis and modelling are strongly LLM-exposed, but original impact research depends on field sampling and defensible methodological choices that a model cannot own.

dwa_title: Design video game features or details.
rationale: Game feel is validated by iterative playtesting against human taste, an evaluation signal models cannot generate internally even though they ideate and prototype quickly.

dwa_title: Respond to customer problems or complaints.
rationale: Chatbots and automated resolution flows already close a large share of routine complaints; escalation, emotional de-escalation and goodwill concessions still pull in humans.

dwa_title: Select tools, equipment, or technologies for use in operations or projects.
rationale: Matching specifications to catalogued tool and technology options is well within model capability; procurement authority and fitness-for-purpose liability keep the final selection with a human.

dwa_title: Create models of engineering designs or methods.
rationale: Building CAD/FEA models and scripting simulations is increasingly tool-assisted; the constraint is choosing abstractions and boundary conditions that make the model valid, which is a judgment call.

dwa_title: Advise others regarding green practices or environmental concerns.
rationale: The knowledge base on green practices is well-documented text that models handle well, but the binding constraint is that advice must be tailored to a client's specific operations and accepted by them, which requires contextual fact-gathering and persuasion.

dwa_title: Determine resource needs.
rationale: Generic resource determination is analytic and highly model-exposed, but the input assumptions are rarely fully documented and the resulting budget commitment is owned by a human manager; wording is too broad for a confident call.

dwa_title: Develop exercise or conditioning programs.
rationale: Commercial fitness and rehab apps already generate individualised conditioning programs algorithmically; what still requires a human is screening for contraindications and adjusting to observed movement quality.

dwa_title: Conduct employee training programs.
rationale: Program authoring, scheduling and assessment are already largely software-mediated; the residual human work is live delivery, cohort engagement and adapting to organisational politics.

dwa_title: Advise others on ways to improve processes or products.
rationale: Improvement ideas can be generated well from data and documentation, but identifying the real bottleneck usually requires observing the process in situ and securing buy-in from the people who must change.

dwa_title: Research industrial processes or operations.
rationale: Documentation and sensor-log analysis are strongly LLM-exposed, but understanding how a plant actually runs requires floor observation and interviews with operators.

dwa_title: Examine records or other types of data to investigate criminal activities.
rationale: Transaction-monitoring and link-analysis systems already flag patterns at scale, but investigative conclusions that trigger legal action must be adopted and defended by an accountable investigator.

dwa_title: Monitor the security of digital information.
rationale: SIEM, EDR and anomaly-detection pipelines already automate detection and triage at scale, but adversarial novelty and the consequences of a missed or mishandled breach keep a named analyst in the escalation loop.

dwa_title: Evaluate plans or specifications to determine technological or environmental implications.
rationale: Reasoning from specifications to downstream technical and environmental consequences is analytic and model-assistable, but it is forecasting under genuine scientific uncertainty where expert engineers legitimately disagree.

dwa_title: Devise research or testing protocols.
rationale: Protocol writing is structured reasoning over prior literature and standards where models perform well, but the design choices carry validity and safety consequences requiring review boards and a responsible investigator.

dwa_title: Coordinate sales campaigns.
rationale: Campaign planning, copy and analytics are highly LLM-exposed, but marshalling a sales team and negotiating priorities across stakeholders remains a coordination role held by a person.

dwa_title: Recommend technical design or process changes to improve efficiency, quality, or performance.
rationale: Design and efficiency recommendations are analytically tractable, but they depend on situated knowledge of the physical system and an engineer who can be held answerable if the change degrades safety or quality.

dwa_title: Review blueprints or specifications to determine work requirements.
rationale: BIM-based quantity takeoff automates parts of this, yet interpreting blueprints against field conditions and code compliance still needs a licensed or experienced human whose misreading has structural consequences.

dwa_title: Estimate green project costs.
rationale: Green retrofit and energy project costing depends on thin, fast-moving data on incentives, technology pricing and site-specific conditions, so model output must be re-based by a human with current market knowledge.

dwa_title: Select resources needed to accomplish tasks.
rationale: An abstract allocation decision that maps well onto model reasoning and optimization tools; ambiguity of the phrasing and reliance on unlogged local availability limit full automation.

dwa_title: Schedule operational activities.
rationale: Operational scheduling is the canonical domain of deployed planning and workforce-management software; human input mainly enters when shifting priorities or staffing disputes break the model's assumptions.

dwa_title: Design research studies to obtain scientific information.
rationale: Study design is reasoning over confounds, power and feasibility that models can draft competently, but the choice of what question is worth asking and the ethical/scientific warrant for the design remain attributed to a named investigator.

dwa_title: Report maintenance or equipment problems to appropriate personnel.
rationale: Sensor telemetry, condition monitoring and automated work-order ticketing already detect and route equipment faults end-to-end; the residual human role is noticing problems that instrumentation does not cover.

dwa_title: Coordinate resource procurement activities.
rationale: E-procurement systems already automate requisition, sourcing and reordering; supplier negotiation and contract commitment remain human-signed.

dwa_title: Plan production or operational procedures or sequences.
rationale: Production sequencing is a mature domain for APS and scheduling optimizers, but equipment quirks, quality and safety consequences keep a process engineer signing off.

dwa_title: Program robotic equipment.
rationale: Path and logic generation can be drafted or synthesized offline, but teaching points, fixturing tolerances and safety validation of a moving machine require on-site commissioning by an accountable engineer.

dwa_title: Explain project details to the general public.
rationale: Drafting the explanation is easy for a model, but the activity typically means facing skeptical stakeholders at public meetings, where credibility and live handling of objections are the actual work.

dwa_title: Recruit personnel.
rationale: Sourcing, outreach copy and resume matching are already heavily tool-driven, but converting passive candidates depends on persuasion and relationship-building by a recruiter.

dwa_title: Maintain the inventory of equipment.
rationale: Asset-tracking software handles the ledger, calibration schedules and reorder alerts; someone must still locate, tag and physically verify equipment, and asset accountability is usually assigned to a named custodian.

dwa_title: Monitor computer system performance to ensure proper operation.
rationale: System observability stacks with automated alerting and self-healing runbooks already own continuous performance monitoring end-to-end in mainstream IT operations.

dwa_title: Maintain student records.
rationale: Student information systems already handle entry, updates and reporting by rule; the remaining constraint is privacy/records-custodian accountability rather than capability.

dwa_title: Research impacts of environmental conservation initiatives.
rationale: Evaluating conservation outcomes hinges on contested counterfactual attribution and field monitoring; models can synthesise evidence but cannot settle the causal claim.

dwa_title: Monitor the productivity or efficiency of industrial operations.
rationale: MES and OEE dashboards already compute and report throughput and efficiency continuously from instrumented lines; the residual human role is interpreting causes and deciding interventions.

dwa_title: Evaluate program effectiveness.
rationale: Data synthesis, indicator construction and report drafting are highly model-exposed, but attributing outcomes to a program and defending that causal claim to stakeholders remains a contested human judgment.

dwa_title: Evaluate effectiveness of personnel policies or practices.
rationale: HR analytics platforms already surface policy impacts on turnover and equity, but legal exposure and employee-relations nuance keep an accountable HR professional in the loop.

dwa_title: Monitor industrial energy consumption or management.
rationale: Metering plus energy-management software performs continuous consumption tracking and anomaly detection end-to-end; humans mainly set targets and act on exceptions.

dwa_title: Communicate technical information to suppliers, contractors, or regulatory agencies.
rationale: Translating and transmitting technical specifications is near-pure information work for a model, yet accuracy of what is certified to regulators or suppliers carries liability requiring a named human attestor.

dwa_title: Assign duties or work schedules to employees.
rationale: The optimization is solved by software, but actually assigning duties is an exercise of supervisory authority over named employees, with labor-relations consequences a system cannot own.

dwa_title: Design layout of art or product exhibits, displays, or promotional materials.
rationale: Generative image and layout tools can produce strong concept options, but the design must be resolved against a real physical space, sightlines and materials, and client taste negotiation anchors the final call to a human.

dwa_title: Evaluate technical data to determine effect on designs or plans.
rationale: Propagating a technical finding through a design requires integrating tacit constraints and code obligations, and in licensed engineering contexts a named professional must sign off on the design change.

dwa_title: Create electrical schematics.
rationale: EDA tools already auto-generate netlists, symbols and routing, and models can draft standard circuits, but code-compliant and safe topology selection still requires qualified human sign-off.

dwa_title: Provide technical guidance to other personnel.
rationale: Explaining technical matter is squarely in a language model's strength, but guiding personnel means diagnosing what the colleague actually misunderstands and staying answerable for the outcome of their work.

dwa_title: Monitor the performance of computer networks.
rationale: Network telemetry is machine-readable and thresholding/alerting is a solved, commercially standard function; humans are only pulled in for remediation decisions, not the monitoring itself.

dwa_title: Issue permits or other legal documents.
rationale: Routine permits are already auto-issued by e-government portals, but conferring legal rights requires a statutorily authorised official to be answerable for the determination.

dwa_title: Maintain repair or maintenance records.
rationale: CMMS platforms automate most of the record structure, but maintenance logs in regulated domains (aviation, medical devices, lifts) legally require a named certifying technician's attestation that the work was actually performed.

dwa_title: Analyze risks to minimize losses or damages.
rationale: Quantitative loss modelling is automatable but tail risks and novel exposures are precisely where models fail; an accountable human underwriter, actuary or risk officer must own the residual judgment.

dwa_title: Establish work standards.
rationale: Drafting standards from observed process data is well within model capability, but the standard only binds if a manager with authority negotiates and ratifies it with the workforce.

dwa_title: Develop sustainable organizational policies or practices.
rationale: Policy text generation is a near-ideal language task, but policy only exists once negotiated and adopted by accountable leadership, which is a relational and governance act rather than a drafting one.

dwa_title: Communicate test or assessment results to medical professionals.
rationale: Automated result routing, critical-value alerting and structured report delivery are already deployed; what still binds is a qualified signatory for interpretation and confirmation that urgent findings were actually received.

dwa_title: Advise others on educational matters.
rationale: Broadly stated educational advising is mostly information synthesis and explanation, well within model range; the constraint is tailoring to a specific learner or institution and being believed.

dwa_title: Monitor resources.
rationale: Generic resource tracking is a data-aggregation and threshold-alert task that dashboards and telemetry already handle, though the vagueness of 'resources' (staff, budget, materials) means some instances require interpretive judgment about adequacy rather than mere counting.

dwa_title: Confer with clients to exchange information.
rationale: Conversational agents already handle routine client information exchange, but eliciting unstated needs and sustaining a trusted commercial relationship keeps a human in the seat for anything non-routine.

dwa_title: Establish operational policies.
rationale: Policy text can be drafted and benchmarked by models, but issuing policy is an exercise of delegated organisational authority with legal exposure that must rest with an identified officer.

dwa_title: Collaborate with others to develop or refine designs.
rationale: Generative and multimodal tools already iterate design variants quickly; what remains human is the shared taste-and-tradeoff negotiation that converges a team on one refined option.

dwa_title: Teach others to use technology or equipment.
rationale: Heterogeneous category: the explanatory layer is highly automatable, but wherever the equipment is physical the trainer must be present to guide hands and verify safe operation.

dwa_title: Design control systems for mechanical or other equipment.
rationale: Control logic is symbolic and code-like, which models handle well, but functional-safety certification and the physical consequences of a mis-tuned loop demand human verification and sign-off.

dwa_title: Implement advertising or marketing initiatives.
rationale: Programmatic ad platforms plus generative creative already execute large parts of campaign launch and optimization; the constraint is brand, budget and legal approval plus coordination with agencies and channel partners.

dwa_title: Develop environmental sustainability plans or projects.
rationale: Sustainability planning is largely analysis and narrative synthesis that models do well, but target-setting requires organisational buy-in and executive ownership of commitments.

dwa_title: Plan environmental research.
rationale: Study design and sampling strategy are text-and-analysis work an LLM handles well, but site conditions, regulatory scope and stakeholder negotiation force a responsible human planner.

dwa_title: Operate computer systems.
rationale: Routine system operation is the classic domain of schedulers, orchestration and RPA; the residual human role is exception handling and authorising privileged actions.

dwa_title: Discuss design or technical features of products or services with technical personnel.
rationale: Models can generate and critique technical design content fluently, but the activity is a live negotiation of shared understanding among engineers, so the human dialogue partner cannot be removed without removing the task itself.

dwa_title: Advise educators on curricula, instructional methods, or policies.
rationale: Curriculum and pedagogy recommendations are text-and-evidence work models do well; adoption hinges on classroom-level context and persuading teachers who must implement it.

dwa_title: Monitor availability of equipment or supplies.
rationale: Inventory and asset-tracking systems with barcodes, RFID and ERP reorder triggers already perform stock-level monitoring end-to-end; the residual human role is physical verification of counts and exception handling.

dwa_title: Advise others on legal or regulatory compliance matters.
rationale: The research-and-drafting core is squarely in frontier-model territory, but compliance advice carries liability that must attach to a named, often licensed, human who signs off on the interpretation.

dwa_title: Analyze design or requirements information for mechanical equipment or systems.
rationale: Mechanical analysis depends on geometry, materials behaviour and failure modes that simulation tools assist with but cannot certify; licensed engineering responsibility anchors the final determination.

dwa_title: Develop operating strategies, plans, or procedures for green or sustainable operations.
rationale: Benchmarking practices and writing strategy documents is squarely in model capability, but the binding constraint is securing organizational buy-in and trading off cost against environmental goals in a contested internal setting.

dwa_title: Plan biological research.
rationale: Models can draft hypotheses, designs, protocols and power calculations from the literature, but the binding constraint is that a named investigator must own feasibility, ethics approval and resource commitments for work involving living systems.

dwa_title: Advise others on business or operational matters.
rationale: Business advice hinges on contested judgment about a specific firm's politics, incentives and private information, and its value comes partly from a trusted adviser relationship rather than the analysis alone.

dwa_title: Gather medical information from patient histories.
rationale: Abstracting structured and narrative data from existing records is close to pure text processing; the binding constraint is clinical accountability for omitted or misread findings.

dwa_title: Review plans or proposals for environmental conservation.
rationale: Conservation plan review weighs contested ecological trade-offs and stakeholder interests against incomplete field data, so models can summarise and flag but cannot settle the scientific judgment call.

dwa_title: Record patient medical histories.
rationale: Ambient AI scribes now draft histories from clinical conversation at scale, but the clinician must elicit and verify the content because an erroneous history propagates into diagnosis and liability.

dwa_title: Conduct research to increase knowledge about medical issues.
rationale: Literature synthesis, hypothesis generation and data analysis are strongly model-exposed, but generating new medical knowledge still binds on wet-lab or clinical data collection and on a named principal investigator answerable for human-subject integrity.

dwa_title: Calculate geographic positions from survey data.
rationale: Coordinate reduction, datum transformation and least-squares network adjustment are solved algorithms running inside standard survey software; only blunder adjudication and certification need a person.

dwa_title: Develop environmental research methods.
rationale: Devising novel sampling and measurement methods requires validating them against messy field reality and instrument behaviour, which no deployed system can close the loop on.

dwa_title: Select project materials.
rationale: Material selection against performance, code and cost criteria is highly analyzable, but samples are often judged in hand and specification errors carry warranty or code-compliance liability requiring a named specifier.

dwa_title: Develop operating strategies, plans, or procedures.
rationale: Strategy and operating plans rest on contested assumptions about an organisation's future and require buy-in from those who must execute them; models accelerate option generation and documentation but cannot commit the organisation.

dwa_title: Interpret cultural or religious information for others.
rationale: Models hold broad cultural and doctrinal knowledge, but conveying meaning that is contested, community-specific and identity-laden depends on standing and trust the speaker holds within that community.

dwa_title: Contact current or potential customers to promote products or services.
rationale: Automated email/SMS sequences and increasingly voice agents already handle high-volume outreach; the binding constraint is customer tolerance and the relationship-building that converts contact into commitment for anything beyond commodity sales.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of mechanical equipment.
rationale: Parametric CAD automates derivative views and drawing sheets from a model, but authoring the geometry itself with correct tolerances and manufacturability remains human-led.

dwa_title: Recommend organizational process or policy changes.
rationale: Models can draft credible policy and process recommendations, but the binding constraint is tacit organizational politics and the need for someone with standing to own and push the change through stakeholders.

dwa_title: Evaluate designs or specifications to ensure quality.
rationale: Rule-based design-rule and specification checking is automated in CAD/EDA toolchains, but quality sign-off is a formal accountability act tied to a responsible reviewer.

dwa_title: Apply knowledge or research findings to address environmental problems.
rationale: Synthesising literature and mapping findings onto a problem is core LLM territory, but translating research into a defensible intervention under ecological uncertainty and contested evidence still needs an accountable expert.

dwa_title: Collect information about clients.
rationale: Digital intake forms and CRM enrichment already capture most structured client data; what remains is the conversational elicitation of context clients do not volunteer.

dwa_title: Explain engineering drawings, specifications, or other technical information.
rationale: Multimodal reading of drawings is still unreliable for dimensioned engineering documents, and the work is a live dialogue calibrated to what a specific tradesperson or client misunderstands, with build errors as the downside.

dwa_title: Advise others about environmental management or conservation.
rationale: Synthesising regulations, site data and best practice is strongly LLM-exposed, but conservation advice rests on contested trade-offs and often on certified sign-off tied to site inspection.

dwa_title: Evaluate effectiveness of educational programs.
rationale: Assessment data mining is mature, but curricular judgment, classroom observation and accreditation defensibility require an educator's sign-off.

dwa_title: Teach physical science or mathematics courses at the college level.
rationale: Technical content is highly formalisable and well covered by models, yet lab supervision, live problem-solving and institutional certification keep an instructor in the loop.

dwa_title: Test computer hardware performance.
rationale: Benchmark suites, burn-in rigs and diagnostic firmware already run and report unattended; humans are needed mainly to rack the hardware and attach instrumentation.

dwa_title: Determine operational methods.
rationale: Highly heterogeneous activity; optimisation software already sets many operational parameters, but choosing methods usually requires tacit knowledge of the specific worksite and buy-in from those who will execute them.

dwa_title: Promote educational institutions or programs.
rationale: Recruitment materials and inquiry handling are highly automatable, but enrolment persuasion involves counselling prospective students and families in person, plus regulated accuracy in representing programmes.

dwa_title: Train sales personnel.
rationale: AI role-play and pitch-critique tools already cover much of the drilling, but sales coaching trades on credibility, motivation and modelling behaviour that a peer or manager supplies.

dwa_title: Analyze patient data to determine patient needs or treatment goals.
rationale: Setting treatment goals is a licensed clinical act tied to patient preferences and consent; models can draft the assessment but scope-of-practice rules bind responsibility to a clinician.

dwa_title: Teach safety standards or environmental compliance methods.
rationale: Much compliance instruction is already delivered as standardised LMS modules, but regulators require a qualified trainer to attest to competency, and hands-on drills and equipment demonstrations still need a body present.

dwa_title: Monitor organizational compliance with regulations.
rationale: Largely document- and data-based, so models can do much of the reading and cross-referencing, yet regulators require an accountable compliance officer to attest and to exercise interpretive discretion.

dwa_title: Determine methods to minimize environmental impact of activities.
rationale: Regulatory synthesis and mitigation-option generation are strongly LLM-exposed, but the tradeoffs among cost, ecology and compliance are contested and permits require a certified professional's attestation.

dwa_title: Plan work operations.
rationale: Scheduling and workload allocation are well served by optimization tools and LLM drafting, but committing people to work requires authority over staff and tacit knowledge of local constraints.

dwa_title: Incorporate green features into the design of structures or facilities.
rationale: Sustainability rating systems and energy-modelling knowledge are highly codified text and calculation, so models can propose measures; the binding constraint is trading off cost, client priorities and certification strategy in a specific project context.

dwa_title: Research genetic characteristics or expression.
rationale: Sequence and expression analysis is heavily computational and highly LLM/ML-exposed, but hypothesis framing plus wet-lab sample handling and assay execution remain hands-on outside a few automated screening facilities.

dwa_title: Coordinate training activities.
rationale: Scheduling, curriculum assembly and enrollment tracking are largely handled by LMS automation, but arranging instructors and reading learner needs keeps a coordinator in the loop.

dwa_title: Evaluate green operations or programs for compliance with standards or regulations.
rationale: Standards conformance for programs is largely evidence-document review that models handle well, but verification of what actually happens operationally requires on-site corroboration and a certifiable human conclusion.

dwa_title: Conduct financial or regulatory audits.
rationale: Analytics already automate sampling, reconciliation and anomaly detection, yet audit opinions are statutorily signed by a licensed individual who bears personal and firm liability for the conclusion.

dwa_title: Evaluate environmental or sustainability projects.
rationale: Evaluation typically requires site verification, stakeholder consultation and weighing contested ecological and social values, none of which a model can discharge or be held answerable for.

dwa_title: Select production input materials.
rationale: ERP/MRP and supplier-optimisation systems already automate routine input selection against specs and cost, but the binding constraint is verifying actual material quality and supply-chain tradeoffs that require physical inspection and vendor negotiation.

dwa_title: Collaborate with others to determine design specifications or details.
rationale: Specification trade-offs can be drafted and explored by a model, but reaching agreement across stakeholders with competing priorities is the binding constraint and remains a human bargaining process.

dwa_title: Identify environmental concerns.
rationale: Screening for known concern categories is pattern-matching a model does well, but spotting unlisted or site-specific hazards requires contextual observation and professional responsibility for what was missed.

dwa_title: Determine operational compliance with regulations or standards.
rationale: Mapping evidence to regulatory text is squarely in reach of language models, but a compliance determination is a legally consequential act that an identified, often licensed, person must own.

dwa_title: Design integrated computer systems.
rationale: Integration design depends on undocumented legacy interfaces, vendor constraints and hardware realities that a model cannot inspect or negotiate on its own.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of industrial production systems.
rationale: Plant layouts and P&IDs must encode verified process logic and safety interlocks, so drafting software accelerates production while an engineer remains the source of truth and the signatory.

dwa_title: Create electronic data backup to prevent loss of information.
rationale: Scheduled snapshotting, replication and cloud backup services are mature commodity automation; the residual human role is defining retention policy and verifying restores.

dwa_title: Evaluate characteristics of products.
rationale: Machine vision and automated test rigs already grade many product attributes, but attributes like feel, taste, durability or fit still require a person handling the item.

dwa_title: Resolve computer network problems.
rationale: AIOps tools detect and sometimes self-heal known fault patterns, but novel outages mix ambiguous telemetry with physical-layer causes (cables, optics, power) that require someone on site to confirm and fix.

dwa_title: Manage budgets for appropriate resource allocation.
rationale: Optimization tools can propose allocations from structured data, but the binding constraint is political negotiation among units and accountability for the resulting cuts.

dwa_title: Teach social science courses at the college level.
rationale: Content generation and assessment drafting are well within model reach; live discussion of contested social questions and grading responsibility anchor a faculty human.

dwa_title: Maintain computer equipment or software.
rationale: The software half (patching, imaging, configuration management) is already heavily scripted and model-assistable, while the equipment half still needs physical hands, so neither side dominates.

dwa_title: Confer with technical personnel to prepare designs or operational plans.
rationale: Specification reconciliation, constraint checking and plan drafting are strongly model-exposed, but sign-off on engineered designs rests with responsible professionals and the conferral resolves genuine technical disagreement.

dwa_title: Teach health management classes.
rationale: Standardised health-education content delivers well through digital programs, but behaviour change in a live class depends on reading group dynamics, motivating participants and tailoring advice to disclosed personal circumstances.

dwa_title: Install computer software.
rationale: Package managers, imaging and MDM/endpoint tooling push software at scale without human touch; exceptions are legacy or physically isolated machines and licensing edge cases.

dwa_title: Design tools, fixtures, or other devices for production equipment.
rationale: Fixture and tooling design is the most rule-bound and library-driven of design tasks, with automated jig generation already in CAM suites; residual work is fitting the tool to an actual machine and part behaviour observed on the floor.

dwa_title: Record research or operational data.
rationale: Digital instrumentation and data-capture systems record most research and operational data without human transcription; manual recording persists where readings or observations are made by hand at the bench or site.

dwa_title: Teach humanities courses at the college level.
rationale: Models handle humanities content and discussion prompts well, but accredited instruction, seminar facilitation and grading authority rest with a credentialed faculty member.

dwa_title: Conduct health or safety training programs.
rationale: Compliance e-learning already delivers much of this at scale, but regulators typically require a named competent person to certify the program and hands-on drills or equipment practice cannot be screen-based.

dwa_title: Evaluate project designs to determine adequacy or feasibility.
rationale: Design adequacy reviews can be heavily assisted by code-checking and simulation, but licensure and liability regimes require a qualified human to attest that the design is sound.

dwa_title: Record vital statistics or other health information.
rationale: Device-to-record interfaces already push vitals automatically, but obtaining the measurement at the bedside and attesting to statutory registry accuracy keeps a licensed human in the chain.

dwa_title: Evaluate the effectiveness of counseling or educational programs.
rationale: Outcome data and survey text can be analysed automatically, but judging counseling efficacy hinges on interpreting participant experience and clinical context that requires human observation.

dwa_title: Locate natural resources using geospatial or other environmental data.
rationale: ML prospectivity mapping over remote-sensing and geophysical stacks is deployed and genuinely productive, but the binding constraint is sparse, noisy ground truth: committing capital to a drill target rests on expert geological inference that models cannot yet own.

dwa_title: Advise athletes, coaches, or trainers on exercise regimens, nutrition, or equipment use.
rationale: Apps already generate training and nutrition plans, but observing movement, fitting equipment and sustaining athlete motivation require in-person presence and rapport.

dwa_title: Design electronic or computer equipment or instrumentation.
rationale: Circuit synthesis, place-and-route and firmware scaffolding are already heavily automated in EDA flows, yet architectural trade-offs, novel requirements and silicon validation still anchor a human designer.

dwa_title: Develop technical specifications for systems or equipment.
rationale: Equipment and system specs often carry engineering-liability weight and must be reconciled with site conditions and codes, so a licensed engineer signs even when the document is machine-drafted.

dwa_title: Manage organizational or project budgets.
rationale: Forecasting, variance analysis and reallocation modelling are highly tractable for software, but trade-off decisions among competing claimants and fiduciary sign-off require a named budget owner.

dwa_title: Evaluate environmental impact of operational or development activities.
rationale: Impact evaluations are contested professional judgments that regulators require a named, often licensed, assessor to stand behind, even though the analytic drafting is highly model-assistable.

dwa_title: Verify accuracy of patient information.
rationale: Automated eligibility checks and record matching help, but confirming identity, demographics and history usually requires interrogating the patient directly and a clinician or registrar is accountable for a misidentification with potentially serious clinical consequences.

dwa_title: Promote environmental sustainability or conservation initiatives.
rationale: Educational materials and messaging generate easily, but changing behaviour and mobilising communities depends on credible human messengers and local presence.

dwa_title: Research diseases or parasites.
rationale: Literature synthesis, epidemiological modelling and genomic analysis are strongly machine-assisted, but culturing pathogens, field sampling and biosafety-regulated experimentation anchor the work to physical labs and licensed investigators.

dwa_title: Develop biological research methods.
rationale: Method development in biology is iterative wet-lab troubleshooting where tacit bench knowledge and physical trial dominate; models accelerate literature-based design but cannot run the optimization loop.

dwa_title: Develop program goals or plans.
rationale: Drafting goals and plans is easy for a model, but goals bind budgets and staff and therefore require legitimacy conferred by an accountable leader negotiating with stakeholders.

dwa_title: Evaluate capabilities or training needs.
rationale: Skills-gap inference from assessments and role profiles is well suited to models; the binding constraint is tacit knowledge of the individual and the organisation's priorities that only surfaces in conversation.

dwa_title: Instruct college students in social sciences or humanities disciplines.
rationale: The intellectual content of humanities and social science teaching is squarely in LLM territory, but accreditation and degree-granting require a named instructor of record who owns assessment and certifies student learning.

dwa_title: Train staff members.
rationale: Content design, curricula and assessments are strongly LLM-exposed and e-learning platforms already carry much of the delivery, but reading learner confusion, motivating staff and certifying competence keeps a human trainer in the loop.

dwa_title: Monitor student performance.
rationale: Learning-management dashboards and automated grading already surface much of the signal, but interpreting a student's trajectory and deciding what it means for them remains a relational, accountable teacher act.

dwa_title: Develop organizational policies or programs.
rationale: Drafting policy text and benchmarking against precedent is highly LLM-exposed, but policy creation requires negotiating stakeholder interests and carries legal and governance liability that an identified officer or board must accept.

dwa_title: Advise patients on effects of health conditions or treatments.
rationale: Explaining prognosis and treatment effects is informed-consent territory: the content is textual but a licensed clinician must own the communication and its interpretation.

dwa_title: Monitor nutrition related activities of individuals or groups.
rationale: Intake logging and nutrient analysis are well handled by software, but verifying what people actually eat and adjusting plans for medical or behavioural realities requires human observation and counselling.

dwa_title: Advise others on matters of public policy.
rationale: Policy analysis and option memos are strongly model-assisted, but the work is irreducibly value-laden and contested, so a named advisor must own the recommendation before decision-makers.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of energy production systems.
rationale: Single-line diagrams and plant schematics for energy systems feed directly into regulated safety and grid-interconnection review, so drafting is assisted but ownership stays with a licensed engineer.

dwa_title: Discuss designs or plans with clients.
rationale: Generative tools can visualise and explain plan options instantly, yet interpreting a client's vague aesthetic or functional preferences and winning their sign-off is relational work.

dwa_title: Maintain supply or equipment inventories.
rationale: Inventory tracking and reorder-point triggering are mature commodity software, but physically verifying, counting and restocking supplies and equipment on site still requires hands, so only the informational half detaches.

dwa_title: Plan experiential learning activities.
rationale: Ideas and lesson scaffolds generate easily, but experiential activities depend on site logistics, safety supervision and knowledge of the specific learner group, which requires a present organiser.

dwa_title: Collaborate with others to resolve information technology issues.
rationale: IT troubleshooting is heavily text- and log-based and increasingly agent-assisted, yet cross-team coordination and system access approvals keep humans in the loop.

dwa_title: Train personnel to enhance job skills.
rationale: Content design, practice scenarios and feedback are highly LLM-exposed, but diagnosing an individual worker's skill gap and motivating them to change behaviour remains a relational act.

dwa_title: Maintain inventories of materials, equipment, or products.
rationale: ERP/WMS systems with barcode and RFID capture already own the record-keeping and replenishment logic; the binding constraint is the physical cycle counting and put-away of materials and products.

dwa_title: Maintain contingency plans for disaster recovery.
rationale: Plan upkeep is largely document reconciliation against changing systems and can be substantially machine-drafted, but currency of the plan depends on tacit knowledge of real dependencies and someone must attest that recovery will actually work.

dwa_title: Determine geographic coordinates.
rationale: GNSS receivers, RTK networks and georeferencing software compute coordinates deterministically; the only residual human element is physically occupying the point and certifying the result where survey law requires a licensed signature.

dwa_title: Advise others on career or personal development.
rationale: The value lies in a trusted developmental relationship and accurate reading of a person's self-presentation over time, which a chatbot can supplement but not own.

dwa_title: Research hydrologic features or processes.
rationale: Literature synthesis and hydrologic model runs are highly machine-assisted, but field gauging and the framing of research questions and model assumptions remain expert-owned.

dwa_title: Create graphical representations of civil structures.
rationale: BIM and detailing tools generate large parts of the drawing set, but civil drawings are permit instruments requiring a licensed engineer's seal, which anchors responsibility to a person.

dwa_title: Advise students on academic or career matters.
rationale: Course selection and career information is easily automated, but the counselling relationship — eliciting a student's real constraints, motivation and distress — is the substance of the work.

dwa_title: Process sales or other transactions.
rationale: Payment rails, POS and e-commerce checkout already execute transactions end-to-end; the only binding constraint is residual cash/physical handling and exception disputes.

dwa_title: Order medical diagnostic or clinical tests.
rationale: Models can propose appropriate test panels well and CDS tools already do so, but a test order is a licensed clinical act tied to a named provider's credential and liability, so autonomy is legally foreclosed.

dwa_title: Evaluate civic projects or public policies.
rationale: Policy evaluation is heavily text-and-data based and thus model-exposed, but it involves contested value tradeoffs and political legitimacy that demand a named human evaluator.

dwa_title: Implement security measures for computer or information systems.
rationale: Policy-as-code, automated patching and managed detection handle much of the mechanics, but risk trade-offs, adversarial ambiguity and regulatory attestation require a named security owner.

dwa_title: Determine operational criteria or specifications.
rationale: Operational criteria encode an organisation's risk appetite and resource constraints, information that is tacit and negotiated rather than retrievable, though models can benchmark and draft the resulting standards.

dwa_title: Prepare accident or incident reports.
rationale: The binding constraint is firsthand observation and witness interviewing at the scene plus the report's use as a legal and insurance record requiring an attesting human author.

dwa_title: Develop safety standards, policies, or procedures.
rationale: Drafting standards text is highly tractable for language models, but the binding constraint is that safety policy must be adopted and signed by an accountable officer with knowledge of site-specific hazards and regulatory exposure.

dwa_title: Merchandise healthcare products or services.
rationale: Content generation, targeting and product positioning are automatable, but regulated healthcare claims and clinician relationships require human oversight and presence.

dwa_title: Provide health and wellness advice to patients, program participants, or caregivers.
rationale: Generic wellness guidance is already delivered by apps and chatbots, but individualised advice tied to a patient's condition triggers clinical accountability and depends on motivational rapport.

dwa_title: Research microbiological or chemical processes or structures.
rationale: High-throughput robotic platforms and predictive models cover slices of the bench work, but end-to-end autonomous laboratories are rare in deployment; sample preparation and troubleshooting keep hands in the loop.

dwa_title: Negotiate prices or other sales terms.
rationale: Dynamic pricing engines and automated haggling bots already set terms in commoditised transactions; the constraint is discretionary concession authority and reading the counterparty in higher-value deals.

dwa_title: Administer tests to assess educational needs or progress.
rationale: Computer-based test delivery and scoring are routine, but proctoring, accommodations and standardized-administration protocols still require a responsible human present.

dwa_title: Customize energy products or services to meet customer needs.
rationale: Configuring energy plans is data-driven analysis that models handle well; the constraint is contract negotiation and regulated disclosures with a customer.

dwa_title: Communicate with government agencies.
rationale: Regulatory correspondence is document-centric and highly draftable, but filings and representations to agencies typically require an authorised, legally liable signatory.

dwa_title: Teach classes in area of specialization.
rationale: Preparation and explanation are strongly model-exposed, but classroom management and credentialed delivery remain human; specialisation may also demand hands-on demonstration.

dwa_title: Manage information technology projects or system activities.
rationale: Much IT project management is documentation, scheduling and status synthesis that tools and LLMs handle well, but tradeoff decisions and team coordination still require an accountable manager.

dwa_title: Coordinate project activities with other personnel or departments.
rationale: Scheduling, status synthesis and cross-team messaging are highly model-exposed, but securing commitment across departments is fundamentally a negotiation between accountable people.

dwa_title: Develop operational methods or processes that use green materials or emphasize sustainability.
rationale: Material substitution can be screened from databases and literature by models, but performance, durability and regulatory compliance of the substitute must be proven through physical testing in the actual process.

dwa_title: Determine design criteria or specifications.
rationale: Setting criteria means reconciling stakeholder needs, cost, regulation and risk tolerance — models can draft and check against standards, but the trade-off choices are owned by a responsible engineer or designer.

dwa_title: Advise others about land management or conservation.
rationale: Land and conservation advice rests on site inspection, local ecological conditions and contested trade-offs between production and preservation, so remote text reasoning can only prepare and support the recommendation.

dwa_title: Monitor facilities or operational systems.
rationale: Building-management and SCADA platforms with alarming perform continuous facility surveillance today; humans are retained mostly for response and for unsensored conditions.

dwa_title: Coordinate activities with suppliers, contractors, clients, or other departments.
rationale: Supply-chain and interdepartmental coordination has substantial automated tooling for the transactional layer; the binding constraint is negotiating exceptions and holding counterparties to commitments.

dwa_title: Train personnel.
rationale: Written at high generality, so the split depends on subject matter; the consistent constraint is that instruction-giving is cheap to automate while judging readiness and building trainee confidence is not.

dwa_title: Manage scientific or technical project resources.
rationale: Resource allocation and tracking are highly structured optimization and reporting tasks, yet commitments to staff, sponsors and grantors must be authorized by a named person.

dwa_title: Design public or employee health programs.
rationale: Program design documents can be largely drafted by a model against evidence-based guidelines, but organisational negotiation, privacy/legal compliance and ownership of participant outcomes require a human sponsor.

dwa_title: Research engineering aspects of biological or chemical processes.
rationale: Models can review process literature, simulate kinetics and propose scale-up parameters, but validating bio/chemical process behaviour requires bench and pilot-plant experimentation that no deployed system runs autonomously.

dwa_title: Advise others on healthcare matters.
rationale: Health advice is information-rich and well within model capability, but the duty of care and regulatory exposure attached to health guidance keeps a licensed human responsible.

dwa_title: Communicate safety or hazard information to others.
rationale: Hazard alerts and toolbox-talk content can be generated automatically, but OSHA-style duties require a named person to have communicated and confirmed comprehension, and failure is life-threatening.

dwa_title: Train others on work processes.
rationale: Process knowledge is documentable and explainable by a model, but transfer usually happens through shoulder-to-shoulder demonstration on the actual workflow and tools.

dwa_title: Determine causes of operational problems or failures.
rationale: Root-cause reasoning is language-tractable when data is complete, but causes usually surface only through on-site inspection, interviewing operators and physically probing the system, which no deployed system does end-to-end.

dwa_title: Evaluate treatment options to guide medical decisions.
rationale: Weighing therapeutic options is almost pure information reasoning that models do well, yet medical licensure and liability require a named prescriber to decide.

dwa_title: Establish standards for products, processes, or procedures.
rationale: Standard-setting is an authoritative act: someone with institutional or regulatory standing must adjudicate competing stakeholder interests and be answerable for the threshold chosen, however well a model drafts the text.

dwa_title: Negotiate contracts for transportation, distribution, or logistics services.
rationale: Freight rate negotiation is the most algorithmically advanced case, with digital marketplaces and automated bidding already closing spot deals, yet contractual commitment and carrier relationships remain human-held.

dwa_title: Manage operations, research, or logistics projects.
rationale: Planning, tracking and optimization of projects are strongly model-assisted, but ownership of stakeholder commitments and reprioritization under disruption stays with a manager.

dwa_title: Monitor alarm systems.
rationale: Alarm detection, verification and dispatch routing are already largely software; the residual human role is liability-driven confirmation of ambiguous or false alarms.

dwa_title: Operate computers or computerized equipment.
rationale: Extremely heterogeneous: console-based operation is scriptable and largely automated, while operating computerized machinery involves loading, monitoring and intervening physically at the equipment.

dwa_title: Develop specifications for new products or processes.
rationale: Novel product specs require committing an organisation to unproven trade-offs and validating against physical and market realities the model cannot test; drafting and consistency checking are heavily assisted.

dwa_title: Determine protocols for medical procedures.
rationale: Models can synthesise guidelines and draft protocol text, but clinical protocols require licensed physician sign-off and institutional review because patient safety liability is non-delegable.

dwa_title: Create new recipes or food presentations.
rationale: Taste, aroma and plating must be iterated by a body in a kitchen; text generation can only propose combinations it cannot evaluate.

dwa_title: Develop health assessment methods or programs.
rationale: Designing screening instruments and programs is evidence-synthesis work suited to models, but clinical validity and population impact require accountable licensed health professionals.

dwa_title: Research geological features or processes.
rationale: Geological interpretation depends on field sampling and outcrop observation plus contested inference from sparse evidence, limiting machines to data processing and image analysis.

dwa_title: Develop sustainable industrial or development methods.
rationale: Designing genuinely new industrial or development methods requires empirical validation in physical process conditions; models can propose and screen options but cannot close the loop on whether a method works at scale.

dwa_title: Plan community programs or activities for the general public.
rationale: An LLM can draft program concepts, schedules and outreach materials, but the binding constraint is reading local community needs and coordinating stakeholders, sponsors and venues in person.

dwa_title: Adjust building climate control systems.
rationale: Building management systems already perform setpoint control and optimization autonomously; only physical valve/damper faults require a technician.

dwa_title: Explain medical procedures or test results to patients or family members.
rationale: Portals already release results with automated explanations, yet interpreting significant findings for a patient is a regulated clinical act requiring a named responsible practitioner.

dwa_title: Develop healthcare quality and safety procedures.
rationale: Drafting protocol text is highly model-exposed, but regulators and accreditation bodies require a named clinical leader to approve procedures on which patient safety depends.

dwa_title: Plan facility layouts or designs.
rationale: Space-planning and adjacency optimisation are well served by generative layout tools, but reconciling workflow, code, client preference and site idiosyncrasy still requires a human owner of the final plan.

dwa_title: Negotiate project specifications.
rationale: Trading off scope, cost and technical feasibility across stakeholders with conflicting priorities is contested judgement that must be owned by someone answerable for delivery.

dwa_title: Assess compliance with environmental laws.
rationale: Compliance assessment typically rests on site observation, sampling and interviews, and the finding carries enforcement consequences that statute assigns to an authorised inspector.

dwa_title: Recommend types of assistive devices.
rationale: Device matching requires physical assessment and fitting of the individual body, and prescription-grade recommendations sit with a licensed therapist or clinician.

dwa_title: Advise others on health and safety issues.
rationale: Standards lookup and hazard explanation are highly text-based, but credible advice depends on observing the actual worksite and on a responsible safety professional attesting to it.

dwa_title: Advise medical personnel regarding healthcare issues.
rationale: Clinical decision support is genuinely strong, but licensure and malpractice liability require a named clinician to stand behind advice that shapes patient care.

dwa_title: Obtain written authorization to perform activities.
rationale: Permit and consent workflows are digitised and largely form-driven, but the authorisation must be sought and attested by a legally identifiable party, and negotiating with a reluctant grantor is relational.

dwa_title: Evaluate characteristics of equipment or systems.
rationale: Instrumented systems can be evaluated from sensor data, but many equipment characteristics only reveal themselves through hands-on inspection and physical test setups at the machine.

dwa_title: Collaborate with technical specialists to resolve design or development problems.
rationale: Models can supply and critique deep technical options, but the collaborative resolution with named specialists who sign off on the engineering choice remains human.

dwa_title: Instruct college students in physical or life sciences.
rationale: Laboratory supervision adds in-person safety responsibility on top of the accreditation requirement for a credentialed instructor, so only lecture content and feedback generation are offloadable.

dwa_title: Design energy-efficient equipment or systems.
rationale: Energy modelling and optimisation tools handle much of the trade-off analysis; the constraint is physical validation and code-compliant sign-off rather than cognitive difficulty.

dwa_title: Confer with others to conduct or arrange operational activities.
rationale: Arranging operations has a substantial bookable, rule-based layer that agents can now handle, but the conferring and trade-off negotiation with counterparties stays human.

dwa_title: Research methods to improve food products.
rationale: Formulation ideation and ingredient-literature search are highly model-exposed, but the decisive evidence comes from physical trials and sensory panels that need matter and human palates.

dwa_title: Train personnel on proper operational procedures.
rationale: Operational procedure training usually ends in a competency sign-off on live equipment, and the verification step requires a qualified observer physically watching the trainee perform.

dwa_title: Examine characteristics or behavior of living organisms.
rationale: Automated behaviour tracking works in instrumented enclosures, but examining organisms generally means handling and inspecting them in varied settings, which deployed systems cannot do.

dwa_title: Plan special events.
rationale: Itineraries, budgets and vendor shortlists are readily machine-drafted, but the binding work is negotiating with suppliers and clients and being on site when contingencies hit.

dwa_title: Communicate with other workers to coordinate activities.
rationale: Scheduling and dispatch systems automate the routine signalling, but the binding constraint is that coordination is a live negotiation between accountable humans about who does what.

dwa_title: Develop organizational goals or objectives.
rationale: Setting organisational direction is an act of authority and commitment; even a perfect draft must be owned by executives or a board who answer to stakeholders for it.

dwa_title: Develop technical methods or processes.
rationale: Broadly worded technical method development typically bottoms out in physical trial and validation in a specific plant or lab, which no deployed system performs autonomously.

dwa_title: Present research results to others.
rationale: Slide and narrative generation is highly exposed, but the act of presenting—fielding challenges, defending methods to a live audience—is a relational performance attributed to a specific researcher.

dwa_title: Refer patients to other healthcare practitioners or health resources.
rationale: A referral is a clinical decision that a licensed practitioner must sign and answer for; delayed or misdirected referrals cause real harm regardless of how well a model can suggest options.

dwa_title: Coordinate software or hardware installation.
rationale: Software deployment orchestration is genuinely automated in mature environments, but hardware placement, vendor and user scheduling, and rollback decisions during failed installs still need a coordinator.

dwa_title: Conduct research of processes in natural or industrial ecosystems.
rationale: Sensor networks and remote sensing automate data capture, but designing the study, siting instruments and interpreting confounded ecosystem dynamics require in-situ presence and contestable expert inference.

dwa_title: Research product safety.
rationale: Standards review, hazard analysis and failure-data mining are model-tractable, but destructive and compliance testing is physical and product-liability regimes require a named, qualified person to stand behind the safety conclusion.

dwa_title: Approve expenditures.
rationale: Rule-based spend approvals are already auto-approved below thresholds, but fiduciary and audit requirements demand a named authorizer with delegated signing authority for anything discretionary.

dwa_title: Maintain professional knowledge or certifications.
rationale: Credentialing bodies attach certification to an identified individual who must personally complete and pass continuing-education requirements; the credential cannot be delegated to a machine regardless of how well it knows the material.

dwa_title: Analyze medical data to determine cause of death.
rationale: Cause-of-death determination is a statutory certification by a named medical examiner or coroner with legal consequences, and often depends on physical examination evidence.

dwa_title: Monitor operational procedures in technical environments to ensure conformance to standards.
rationale: Digital procedure execution and audit trails automate conformance checking where work is logged, but observing whether people actually follow protocol in situ, and attesting to it, stays with a human.

dwa_title: Establish rules or policies governing student behavior.
rationale: Model can generate conduct codes, but legitimacy with students, parents and school boards depends on a named educator's authority and relational standing, which cannot be delegated to software.

dwa_title: Develop fire safety or prevention programs or plans.
rationale: Fire plans follow codified codes that LLMs handle well, but they require on-site inspection of building conditions and sign-off by a licensed fire protection professional or marshal.

dwa_title: Develop plans to manage natural or renewable resources.
rationale: Resource management plans depend on locally observed stock conditions and irreducibly contested trade-offs among competing users, with statutory decision authority resting on an agency official.

dwa_title: Design industrial equipment.
rationale: CAD plus topology/generative optimisation automates sizing and detailing of components, but integrating manufacturability, maintenance access and plant-floor realities requires a responsible designer.

dwa_title: Develop emergency procedures.
rationale: Drafting procedures against codes and hazard scenarios is highly text-tractable, but emergency plans must be validated against a specific site and are legally attributable to a named safety officer or authority having jurisdiction.

dwa_title: Establish nursing policies or standards.
rationale: Drafting and harmonizing policy text against regulation and evidence is highly language-shaped, but adoption requires negotiation with clinical staff and a licensed nursing leader who owns the patient-safety consequences.

dwa_title: Communicate detailed medical information to patients or family members.
rationale: Content can be drafted and tailored by a model, but informed consent and disclosure of diagnosis legally attach to a licensed clinician who must read and respond to the patient's emotional state in real time.

dwa_title: Apply new technologies to improve work processes.
rationale: Models can identify and configure candidate technologies, but actually inserting them into a live workflow requires physical/system integration and retraining people, which stalls end-to-end automation.

dwa_title: Assist engineers or scientists with research.
rationale: Heterogeneous support role: literature and data-analysis components are highly exposed, but much assisting involves bench or field work under a scientist's direction.

dwa_title: Coordinate operational activities with external stakeholders.
rationale: Scheduling and status synchronization across organizations is increasingly systemized, but resolving conflicting priorities between independent parties requires someone with authority to commit resources.

dwa_title: Monitor processes for compliance with standards.
rationale: Instrumented processes with statistical process control are already largely self-monitoring; the residual human role is interpreting drift and authorising deviations.

dwa_title: Plan programs to address community health issues.
rationale: Needs assessment and program drafting are text-heavy and LLM-amenable, but community buy-in, coalition building and public accountability for health outcomes make the relationship the substance of the work.

dwa_title: Negotiate sales or lease agreements for products or services.
rationale: Models can price, draft and simulate concessions, but binding a counterparty to terms requires authority to commit the organisation and a signatory who bears the legal consequences.

dwa_title: Train personnel in technical or scientific procedures.
rationale: Technical and scientific procedure training typically hinges on supervised hands-on demonstration and correction at the bench or machine, which caps what screen-delivered instruction can replace.

dwa_title: Coordinate operational activities.
rationale: Broadly stated coordination is largely information routing and scheduling that tools do well, but the binding constraint is getting people to act, which requires a person with standing.

dwa_title: Design industrial processing systems.
rationale: Process simulation and flowsheet software carries much of the computation, but selecting unit operations under uncertain feedstock, safety and economic assumptions remains an engineer's call with hazard liability attached.

dwa_title: Investigate the environmental impact of projects.
rationale: Impact assessment is a regulated act whose findings must be certified by a qualified professional after site inspection and stakeholder consultation, regardless of how much analysis is automated.

dwa_title: Negotiate contracts with clients or service providers.
rationale: Clause analysis and counter-offer generation are strong AI territory, and autonomous procurement negotiation bots exist for tail spend, but strategic client relationships and contractual liability keep a named human in charge.

dwa_title: Monitor performance of organizational members or partners.
rationale: Activity and output metrics are trivially instrumented, but appraising a person's performance carries employment-law and fairness consequences that a named supervisor must own, and much of the signal comes from relational context invisible to systems.

dwa_title: Deliver promotional presentations to current or prospective customers.
rationale: Preparing the deck is near-fully automatable, but live delivery requires reading a room and responding to objections in real time, which buyers still expect from a human representative.

dwa_title: Interview employees, customers, or others to collect information.
rationale: Automated survey and chat interviews already harvest routine information, but eliciting candid or sensitive testimony depends on rapport, probing and reading the respondent, which conversational agents do poorly in adversarial or emotional settings.

dwa_title: Develop environmental remediation or protection plans.
rationale: Remediation plans are regulatory documents that must be stamped by a licensed engineer or geologist and rest on site characterisation data gathered in the field.

dwa_title: Liaise between departments or other groups to improve function or communication.
rationale: The substance is brokering trust and surfacing tacit friction between groups, which requires standing in a live relational position; LLMs can draft the memos and summarise cross-team status but cannot hold the boundary-spanning role.

dwa_title: Prescribe medications.
rationale: Drug selection, dosing and interaction checking are heavily algorithmic already, yet prescriptive authority is statutorily tied to a named licensed prescriber and errors can be lethal and irreversible.

dwa_title: Assess locations for potential green technology installations.
rationale: Solar/wind siting analytics from GIS, LIDAR and irradiance data are commercially strong, but final suitability requires on-site structural, shading and interconnection verification signed by an engineer.

dwa_title: Evaluate patient outcomes to determine effectiveness of treatments.
rationale: Outcome tracking over structured records is highly amenable to model analysis, but attributing improvement to a treatment and acting on it is a licensed clinical judgment.

dwa_title: Design energy production or management equipment or systems.
rationale: Load modelling and equipment selection are computationally tractable, yet grid/utility interconnection standards and high-consequence failure modes keep a licensed engineer accountable for the design.

dwa_title: Establish standards for medical care.
rationale: Care standards carry medico-legal force and must be promulgated by credentialed clinicians answerable for patient harm, even though evidence synthesis and drafting are strongly LLM-exposed.

dwa_title: Collect information from people through observation, interviews, or surveys.
rationale: Surveys are already fully instrumented, but direct observation requires presence and interviewing depends on rapport and adaptive probing that automated instruments handle shallowly.

dwa_title: Design electrical equipment or systems.
rationale: Code-compliance calculations and schematic generation are increasingly tool-assisted, but electrical designs carry fire and shock liability that statutorily requires a stamped, accountable engineer.

dwa_title: Resolve operational performance problems.
rationale: Diagnosis of performance shortfalls is highly analysable from data, but implementing fixes usually requires directing people and physical processes, and someone must answer for the operational outcome.

dwa_title: Collect information about community health needs.
rationale: Secondary epidemiological and administrative data can be mined automatically, but the binding constraint is eliciting needs from residents and community organisations, which requires presence and trust-building.

dwa_title: Design environmental control systems.
rationale: Parametric and simulation tools automate large parts of HVAC/emission control system sizing, but code compliance and stamped engineering drawings bind the work to a licensed human.

dwa_title: Confer with coworkers to coordinate work activities.
rationale: Peer-to-peer work coordination depends on reciprocal human commitment and tacit context; software can only schedule and notify around it.

dwa_title: Guide class discussions.
rationale: The binding constraint is real-time multi-party facilitation: reading who is disengaged, managing conflict and drawing out reticent participants in a shared room, which no deployed system does, even though LLMs handle Socratic dialogue one-to-one well.

dwa_title: Conduct eligibility or selection interviews.
rationale: Asynchronous AI screening interviews are deployed but the substance is live probing and rapport with a person whose benefits or job hang on it, and discrimination law constrains automated scoring.

dwa_title: Design systems to reduce harmful emissions.
rationale: Emissions-control design is heavily model-assisted, but regulatory certification and liability for exceedances legally anchor responsibility to a named engineer.

dwa_title: Research human performance or health factors related to engineering or design activities.
rationale: Human-factors evidence is generated by observing and testing real people, so recruitment, instrumented trials and ethical oversight anchor it to humans even though the synthesis is model-exposed.

dwa_title: Monitor operational activities to ensure compliance with regulations or standard operating procedures.
rationale: Observing whether people actually follow SOPs in live operations demands presence and situational reading that logs and cameras only partially capture.

dwa_title: Diagnose equipment malfunctions.
rationale: Onboard fault codes and diagnostic software narrow the field, but confirming a malfunction requires sensory and manual access to the machine — disassembly, measurement, listening and feeling — that remains human.

dwa_title: Design water conservation systems.
rationale: Hydrologic modelling and design software can generate options, but site-specific constraints, regulatory sign-off and stakeholder water rights require a responsible engineer; the binding constraint is professional accountability for a physically deployed system.

dwa_title: Process x-rays or other medical images.
rationale: Image processing is now overwhelmingly digital and pipeline-driven; residual human work is quality checking and handling of physical media or patient positioning.

dwa_title: Advise communities or institutions regarding health or safety issues.
rationale: Community health and safety guidance is as much about trust, local context and public credibility as about content; an accountable official or professional must deliver and defend it.

dwa_title: Prescribe treatments or therapies.
rationale: Treatment planning is well within model reasoning range, but prescribing is a scope-of-practice act requiring a licensed, identifiable clinician who bears malpractice liability for patient harm.

dwa_title: Sell products or services.
rationale: E-commerce and recommendation engines already close simple transactions end-to-end, but consultative and high-value selling still turns on trust built between people.

dwa_title: Assess educational needs of students.
rationale: Adaptive diagnostics identify skill gaps well, but distinguishing disability, motivation, language and home-context causes requires relational observation and carries placement liability.

dwa_title: Troubleshoot equipment or systems operation problems.
rationale: Troubleshooting is an interactive loop of hypothesis, physical test and reconfiguration on the equipment itself; automated diagnostics assist the hypothesis step but cannot execute the manipulation.

dwa_title: Confer with other personnel to resolve design or operational problems.
