rationale: The technical reasoning is well within model reach, but the activity is definitionally a negotiated exchange among colleagues who must converge on and own a design decision.

dwa_title: Manage financial activities of the organization.
rationale: Organization-wide financial stewardship carries statutory certification and fiduciary liability (e.g. officer attestation), so a human officer must own it even when analysis is machine-generated.

dwa_title: Inform medical professionals regarding patient conditions and care.
rationale: Clinical handoff content is highly summarisable from the record, but a licensed clinician must be answerable for what is conveyed and for the judgment about what matters, so the model can prepare but not own the communication.

dwa_title: Develop treatment plans that use non-medical therapies.
rationale: Non-medical therapeutic planning rests on a sustained therapeutic alliance and weakly codified evidence, so the practitioner's read of the person, not information retrieval, is the limiting input.

dwa_title: Design structures or facilities.
rationale: Parametric and generative design tools produce viable options quickly, yet the binding constraints are client negotiation, site-specific constraints and permit-stage sign-off by a licensed professional.

dwa_title: Confer with organizational members to accomplish work activities.
rationale: Conferring is the relationship itself — mutual commitment among organisational members — so tools can prepare and minute it but not replace the participants.

dwa_title: Plan natural resources conservation or restoration programs.
rationale: Conservation planning hinges on contested ecological judgment, field reconnaissance and negotiation among landowners, agencies and stakeholders rather than on document production.

dwa_title: Check quality of diagnostic images.
rationale: Automated artifact and exposure QC software is deployed, but deciding a study is non-diagnostic and repeating it requires the patient present and a clinically accountable operator.

dwa_title: Implement design or process improvements.
rationale: Designing the improvement is model-tractable but putting it into production touches equipment, procedures and people on the floor, and a responsible engineer or supervisor must validate the changed process.

dwa_title: Develop treatment plans for patients or clients.
rationale: Models can draft coherent, guideline-consistent plans, but licensure and duty-of-care mean a named professional must author and sign the plan, and plan quality depends on relational elicitation of the client's goals and constraints.

dwa_title: Negotiate contracts for environmental remediation, green energy, or renewable resources.
rationale: These deals bundle regulatory liability, long-horizon environmental risk and multi-party public stakeholders, so terms must be judged and signed by an accountable professional rather than generated.

dwa_title: Design psychological or educational treatment procedures or programs.
rationale: Treatment protocol design sits inside clinical licensure and duty of care; a licensed practitioner must own the diagnostic formulation and the risk of harm even when a model drafts the protocol.

dwa_title: Design civil structures or systems.
rationale: Analysis and code-checking are increasingly software-driven, but civil and structural designs must be sealed by a licensed engineer who bears legal liability for public safety.

dwa_title: Collect medical information from patients, family members, or other medical professionals.
rationale: Automated intake handles routine history-taking, but eliciting reluctant, distressed or inconsistent accounts from patients and families is a relational clinical skill with direct safety consequences.

dwa_title: Support the professional development of others.
rationale: Models can generate development plans and feedback text, but mentoring depends on sustained relational credibility, sponsorship and organisational standing that software does not hold.

dwa_title: Design alternative energy systems.
rationale: Solar/wind layout and sizing software already automates much of the configuration, but site assessment, grid interconnection approval and a stamped design require a licensed engineer.

dwa_title: Design electromechanical equipment or systems.
rationale: EDA and generative CAD tools accelerate topology and component selection, but integrating mechanical motion, thermal and safety constraints requires physical prototyping and a licensed engineer's sign-off on the final design.

dwa_title: Establish treatment goals.
rationale: Goal-setting is a collaborative act of eliciting and calibrating a patient's own aspirations against clinical realism; the shared commitment is the deliverable and cannot be outsourced to a system.

dwa_title: Consult with others regarding safety or health equipment or facilities.
rationale: Regulatory codes and equipment specs are highly retrievable text, but safety consultation carries named liability and often requires site-specific observation, anchoring it to an accountable person.

dwa_title: Develop medical treatment plans.
rationale: Medical treatment planning is squarely within LLM reasoning reach as drafting, yet prescribing authority and malpractice liability legally bind the decision to a licensed physician.

dwa_title: Train medical providers.
rationale: Curriculum design and didactic content are already largely machine-generatable and CME e-learning is deployed at scale, but competency sign-off, bedside/procedural coaching and accreditation responsibility bind the activity to a credentialed instructor.

dwa_title: Analyze chemical compounds or substances.
rationale: Automated analyzers and chemometric software handle instrument runs and spectral matching, but sample preparation, handling and method selection remain hands-on in a lab, and results affecting safety or regulatory compliance need a signing analyst.

dwa_title: Collaborate on research activities with scientists or technical specialists.
rationale: The substance is sustained peer collaboration — negotiating design choices and dividing labour with colleagues — which a model can support intellectually but cannot be a party to.

dwa_title: Maintain inventory of medical supplies or equipment.
rationale: Par-level tracking and auto-reordering are solved in software, but counting, stocking, rotating expired stock and locating items in clinical space still needs hands on the shelf.

dwa_title: Supervise student research or internship work.
rationale: Models can critique drafts and suggest methods, but mentorship, research-integrity responsibility and institutional evaluation of the trainee rest with a named supervisor.

dwa_title: Present medical research reports.
rationale: Clinical findings presented to peers or regulators carry authorship liability and require live defense of methodology; drafting support is strong but the speaker must own the claims.

dwa_title: Monitor activities affecting environmental quality.
rationale: Remote sensing and permit data flag likely violations, but linking observed activity to regulatory consequence requires site verification and a legally accountable officer.

dwa_title: Develop new or advanced products or production methods.
rationale: Genuine novelty requires physical prototyping, market judgment and iterative experimentation; ideation support is real but the development cycle itself is not automatable end-to-end.

dwa_title: Design materials for industrial or commercial applications.
rationale: Computational materials design and generative simulation tools accelerate candidate generation, but selection still hinges on physical synthesis, characterisation and failure testing that no deployed system closes the loop on.

dwa_title: Coordinate safety or regulatory compliance activities.
rationale: Compliance and safety regimes typically designate a responsible officer by statute; automated monitoring and tracking assist, but liability for lapses cannot be transferred to software.

dwa_title: Evaluate performance of applicants, trainees, or employees.
rationale: Automated scoring of applicants and trainees exists but is legally constrained by anti-discrimination and adverse-impact rules that demand a human decision-maker of record.

dwa_title: Collaborate with other agencies and institutions to coordinate educational matters.
rationale: Inter-agency coordination is institutional relationship work with competing mandates and political sensitivities; models can prepare agendas and reconcile documents but not represent the institution.

dwa_title: Direct design or development activities.
rationale: Models can generate and critique design options, but setting direction amid conflicting requirements and holding a team to it is a trust-and-authority function.

dwa_title: Conduct anthropological or archaeological research.
rationale: Excavation and ethnographic fieldwork are irreducibly embodied and relational; only the literature review, artefact classification and write-up stages are meaningfully machine-assisted.

dwa_title: Record agricultural or forestry inventory data.
rationale: The recording step is trivially digital, but generating the inventory figures for crops, livestock or timber still depends on in-field observation, counting and measurement; remote sensing covers only part of it.

dwa_title: Train caregivers or other non-medical personnel.
rationale: Instructional content is easy to generate, but confirming that an anxious, often untrained caregiver can actually perform care tasks safely requires observation in situ and clinical responsibility.

dwa_title: Monitor environmental impacts of production or development activities.
rationale: Continuous sensing and telemetry automate the data capture, but interpreting anomalies against permit conditions and doing site verification still requires a qualified person on the ground.

dwa_title: Design energy-efficient vehicles or vehicle components.
rationale: Generative design and CFD/FEA optimisation accelerate component design, but prototyping, validation testing and safety homologation keep engineers in ownership of the outcome.

dwa_title: Develop strategies or programs for students with special needs.
rationale: Special-needs planning is statutorily governed (IEP-type processes) and built from direct observation of the child plus negotiation with families and specialists, so a credentialed human must author and be answerable for it.

dwa_title: Investigate system, equipment, or product failures.
rationale: Log analytics and diagnostic models can localize many failures, but root-cause work usually needs physical teardown and inspection plus a defensible causal judgment, so the machine contribution is hypothesis generation rather than closure.

dwa_title: Manage human resources activities.
rationale: Employment decisions carry legal exposure and the substance is handling people—grievances, discipline, hiring—so a responsible human must remain in place even where systems draft and screen.

dwa_title: Direct quality control activities.
rationale: Automated inspection and SPC systems catch defects, but sign-off on releases, corrective actions and regulatory conformity is a named quality manager's duty.

dwa_title: Direct financial operations.
rationale: Financial control carries fiduciary and statutory certification duties (e.g., officer attestation), so directing operations cannot be delegated to a system despite heavy analytic automation.

dwa_title: Advise others on management of emergencies or hazardous situations or materials.
rationale: Emergency and hazmat guidance is time-critical, situation-specific and often requires on-scene sensing and command authority; the life-safety error cost blocks unsupervised automation even where reference data is codified.

dwa_title: Diagnose medical conditions.
rationale: Frontier models match or beat clinicians on vignette reasoning, yet physical examination, history elicitation and statutory licensure mean the diagnostic act legally belongs to a named clinician.

dwa_title: Monitor operational quality or safety.
rationale: Instrumented quality and safety metrics are readily machine-monitored, but the safety dimension carries a named-responsible-person requirement and depends on unmeasured, in-person cues; the activity as written is heterogeneous.

dwa_title: Inspect operational processes.
rationale: Instrumented processes already self-monitor via SCADA and machine vision, but detecting the anomalies that no sensor covers still needs a person walking the line and interpreting context.

dwa_title: Maintain computer hardware.
rationale: Firmware updates and remote diagnostics are automatable, but swapping drives, cards and cables and racking hardware still requires a person at the machine.

dwa_title: Modify treatment plans to accommodate client needs.
rationale: The substance is negotiating adherence, preferences and life circumstances with the client, and any deviation from the standard plan must be justified by an accountable practitioner.

dwa_title: Communicate with management or other staff to resolve problems.
rationale: The substance is organisational dialogue and alignment with managers; tools can summarise and draft but cannot be the party to an internal negotiation.

dwa_title: Coordinate construction or installation activities.
rationale: Scheduling and clash-detection software handles much of the coordination logic, but reconciling trades and resolving on-site conflicts remains a negotiation among people.

dwa_title: Prescribe assistive medical devices or related treatments.
rationale: Prescribing is a licensed act requiring a named clinician's signature, and device selection depends on hands-on assessment of the patient's body and function; a model can propose options but cannot own the order.

dwa_title: Assess equipment functioning.
rationale: Condition-monitoring sensors and predictive-maintenance analytics cover much of the routine assessment, yet confirming a fault typically still requires physically handling or testing the machine.

dwa_title: Develop technical processes to improve the efficiency of biofuel production.
rationale: Process-efficiency gains in biofuel depend on wet-lab experimentation and pilot-plant iteration with living systems; models can propose hypotheses but cannot close the empirical loop.

dwa_title: Design micro- or nano-scale materials, devices, or systems.
rationale: Nanoscale design is bound by fabrication constraints and process-specific tacit knowledge discovered in cleanroom iteration; models help with parameter search and literature synthesis but cannot own the design-fabricate-measure cycle.

dwa_title: Coordinate cross-disciplinary research programs.
rationale: Synthesising across disciplines is where LLMs are strongest, yet the work is mainly brokering between specialists, funders and institutions, which requires standing and relationships.

dwa_title: Manage preparation of special meals or diets.
rationale: Therapeutic menu planning against dietary restrictions is well-handled by software, but overseeing actual food preparation and allergen safety demands physical supervision and a clinically responsible person.

dwa_title: Develop agricultural methods.
rationale: Method development rests on empirical field trials in specific soils, climates and crops; models can synthesize agronomic literature and design protocols but cannot generate the site-specific evidence that validates a method.

dwa_title: Attend training sessions or professional meetings to develop or maintain professional knowledge.
rationale: Attendance is itself the deliverable — credit hours and peer contact are credited to a present person; models can summarise proceedings but cannot substitute for the attendee.

dwa_title: Assist clients in handling details of daily life.
rationale: Scheduling, form-filling and benefits navigation are highly LLM-exposed, but the work is anchored in a trusted ongoing relationship with a dependent person and frequent errands in the physical world.

dwa_title: Assess skin or hair conditions.
rationale: Image-based dermatological and trichological classifiers are commercially deployed and accurate on common presentations, but palpation, lighting control and triage responsibility keep a person in the loop.

dwa_title: Participate in staffing decisions.
rationale: Participation in a decision is inherently a claim of organisational responsibility and negotiation among stakeholders; analytics can inform but cannot hold the seat.

dwa_title: Verify that medical activities or operations meet standards.
rationale: Verification of clinical standards is an attestation act under professional licensure; the binding constraint is legal responsibility for patient harm, not analytic capability.

dwa_title: Test green technologies or processes.
rationale: Testing novel or immature technologies requires designing bespoke physical trials and interpreting ambiguous performance data; only the analysis and reporting layer is readily machine-handled.

dwa_title: Supervise information technology personnel.
rationale: Ticket routing, workload dashboards and code review tooling automate the monitoring layer, but personnel evaluation, prioritisation conflicts and accountability for system outages rest with a human manager.

dwa_title: Select medical equipment for addressing patient needs.
rationale: Matching equipment to a specific patient's anatomy, function and tolerance requires in-person assessment and fitting, and a licensed clinician must own the selection for safety and liability reasons.

dwa_title: Evaluate characteristics of archival or historical objects.
rationale: Provenance, authenticity and condition assessment rests on tacit connoisseurship plus hands-on material inspection; models can supply comparative research but not the physical appraisal.

dwa_title: Evaluate employee performance.
rationale: Models can aggregate metrics and draft appraisal narratives, but employment law, fairness challenges and the supervisory relationship require a named manager to own the rating.

dwa_title: Administer standardized physical or psychological tests.
rationale: Computer-delivered testing is mature, but standardised protocols for physical measures and proctored psychological instruments require a present, credentialed administrator to preserve validity.

dwa_title: Collaborate with outside groups to develop programs or projects.
rationale: Joint program development with outside organizations rests on trust-building, negotiation and shared commitment between institutions; AI can draft proposals and synthesize inputs but cannot hold the relationship or bind the parties.

dwa_title: Confer with other professionals to plan patient care.
rationale: Care planning is a licensed, negotiated professional act where named clinicians accept liability for the plan; decision support can propose options but the conferral itself is legally lodged in humans.

dwa_title: Supervise laboratory work.
rationale: LIMS automation covers workflow tracking and QC flagging, but a designated laboratory director must certify protocol adherence, troubleshoot bench anomalies in person and sign off on results.

dwa_title: Select staff, team members, or performers.
rationale: Final selection is contested judgment about fit and potential with legal fairness exposure; the binding constraint is who answers for the choice, not scoring capability.

dwa_title: Examine condition of property or products.
rationale: Machine vision handles repeatable product defect inspection on a line, but examining varied property in situ still needs someone walking the site and lifting covers.

dwa_title: Diagnose neural or psychological disorders.
rationale: Psychiatric and neuropsychological diagnosis rests on clinical observation of affect and behaviour within a therapeutic relationship, with contested criteria and licensure-bound liability.

dwa_title: Conduct validation tests of equipment or processes.
rationale: Automated test rigs and scripted protocols execute the runs and models can draft protocols and reports, but in regulated validation (IQ/OQ/PQ, GxP) a named human must approve the acceptance decision.

dwa_title: Analyze laboratory specimens to detect abnormalities or other problems.
rationale: High-throughput analysers and image-based screening already automate much of the detection step, but specimen handling plus regulated result verification and sign-off keep a certified technologist or pathologist in the loop.

dwa_title: Direct fundraising or financing activities.
rationale: Securing donors or capital is fundamentally a trust-based relational sale; AI drafts prospect research and appeals but the ask depends on a person.

dwa_title: Teach exercise or fitness techniques.
rationale: App-based programming and computer-vision form feedback are commercially deployed, yet correcting technique to prevent injury and sustaining client motivation remain embodied and relational.

dwa_title: Inspect products or operations to ensure that standards are met.
rationale: Machine-vision and in-line gauging handle high-volume product inspection well, but heterogeneous items, tactile checks and operational context still require an inspector physically present.

dwa_title: Maintain equipment or systems to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Written broadly enough to include automated monitoring and self-healing systems, but the corrective action still typically requires a technician physically present.

dwa_title: Analyze geological samples.
rationale: Instrumental assay (XRF, XRD, automated mineralogy) is automated, but sample preparation, thin-section handling and petrographic description require hands on rock, which anchors the activity physically even though the interpretive write-up is model-exposed.

dwa_title: Advocate for individual or community needs.
rationale: Drafting arguments and briefs is highly LLM-exposed, but advocacy derives its force from a legitimate human speaking on someone's behalf before other humans.

dwa_title: Monitor environmental conditions to detect hazards.
rationale: Continuous gas, radiation and air-quality sensor networks automate detection well; the binding constraint is deploying and calibrating instruments in situ and owning the hazard call.

dwa_title: Monitor medical facility activities to ensure adherence to standards or regulations.
rationale: Requires walking clinical areas, observing staff practice and interpreting accreditation standards under licensure; patient-safety accountability cannot be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Monitor video displays of medical equipment to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Device self-diagnostics and central telemetry already flag malfunctions automatically, but alarm interpretation and the bedside response remain a licensed clinician's responsibility given the lethality of a missed fault.

dwa_title: Collaborate with other professionals to assess client needs or plan treatments.
rationale: Multidisciplinary needs assessment turns on reconciling divergent professional readings of an ambiguous case, and each discipline signs for its own contribution.

dwa_title: Direct facility maintenance or repair activities.
rationale: CMMS platforms automate work-order generation and prioritisation, but assigning, inspecting and signing off on physical repairs requires presence and a responsible supervisor.

dwa_title: Analyze biological samples.
rationale: Automated liquid handling and assay platforms cover routine sample processing, but preparation of non-standard samples and troubleshooting anomalous runs still demand bench hands and expert oversight.

dwa_title: Direct organizational operations, projects, or services.
rationale: General organisational direction is the exercise of delegated authority over resources and people; capability aside, fiduciary and governance norms require an identifiable human principal.

dwa_title: Measure environmental characteristics.
rationale: Instrumented and telemetered measurement is routine, but field sampling at unmonitored locations still requires someone to carry and operate the equipment.

dwa_title: Attend events to develop professional knowledge.
rationale: The value lies in bodily presence and professional networking at the event; no system can attend on a person's behalf even though it can digest the published content afterwards.

dwa_title: Lead classes or community events.
rationale: Leading a live class or community event requires physical presence, group energy management and real-time crowd reading that no deployed system provides.

dwa_title: Evaluate quality of materials or products.
rationale: Machine-vision and sensor-based inspection is already routine on production lines; what remains human is sampling odd cases, tactile or sensory checks, and disposition of borderline defects.

dwa_title: Supervise workers performing environmentally sustainable activities.
rationale: Compliance checklists and sensor-based monitoring can be automated, but directing crews in the field and attesting to environmental practice requires a present, accountable supervisor.

dwa_title: Maintain electronic equipment.
rationale: Routine cleaning, testing, calibration and part replacement of electronic gear are physical tasks in situ; AI contributes fault interpretation and record-keeping only.

dwa_title: Monitor operations to ensure compliance with safety or security policies or regulations.
rationale: Sensors and video analytics catch some violations, but safety and security oversight involves confronting behaviour in situ and carries statutory liability that attaches to a person.

dwa_title: Demonstrate activity techniques or equipment use.
rationale: Demonstration means performing the motion or operation bodily so a learner can imitate it; video can substitute for generic cases but not for adapting the demo to the individual in the room.

dwa_title: Direct environmental development activities.
rationale: Environmental program direction turns on contested evidence, regulatory sign-off and stakeholder negotiation; analysis and reporting are the only cleanly automatable slices.

dwa_title: Serve on institutional or departmental committees.
rationale: Committee service is constituted by representation and deliberation among named members; an AI can prepare briefs and minutes but cannot hold a seat or a vote.

dwa_title: Repair electronic equipment.
rationale: Board-level fault tracing, soldering and component replacement need fine manipulation and test instruments in hand; the constraint is embodiment, not diagnostic reasoning.

dwa_title: Inspect finished products to locate flaws.
rationale: Machine-vision and anomaly-detection inspection is mature and running unattended on production lines; the residual constraint is handling/presentation of parts and rare defect classes outside the training distribution.

dwa_title: Direct technical activities or operations.
rationale: Operational direction is increasingly instrumented by control and workflow systems, but technical authority over live operations carries safety and regulatory responsibility that names a person.

dwa_title: Direct department activities.
rationale: Departmental direction bundles staffing, discipline and resource allocation over identified employees — decisions an organisation must attribute to a responsible manager.

dwa_title: Teach life skills or strategies to clients or their families.
rationale: Content can be generated and even delivered conversationally, but tailoring to family dynamics and securing buy-in is relational work carried by a responsible practitioner.

dwa_title: Supervise engineering or other technical personnel.
rationale: Technical review can be heavily assisted, but professional engineering responsibility and the authority to direct and appraise staff must attach to an identifiable licensed manager.

dwa_title: Test performance of electrical, electronic, mechanical, or integrated systems or equipment.
rationale: Built-in self-test, automated test equipment and telemetry diagnostics cover much of the measurement, yet hooking up probes and fixturing non-instrumented hardware still requires hands.

dwa_title: Hire personnel.
rationale: Employment-law exposure and the contractual nature of an offer require a named manager to own the decision, regardless of how well models rank candidates.

dwa_title: Operate cash registers.
rationale: Self-checkout and card/mobile payment systems have already displaced the transactional core; what remains is item handling, age checks and cash-drawer custody at the physical point of sale.

dwa_title: Maintain laboratory or technical equipment.
rationale: Calibration and servicing of instruments must be performed and certified on the bench; accreditation regimes require a named technician's calibration record even where data analysis is automated.

dwa_title: Test materials, solutions, or samples.
rationale: Automated sampling and instrumentation handle routine standardized assays well, but sample preparation, loading and non-standard matrices still demand hands in the lab.

dwa_title: Test products for functionality or quality.
rationale: Automated test rigs and machine-vision inspection are mature on high-volume production lines, but fixturing, low-volume or novel products, and functional edge cases still require a technician.

dwa_title: Attend conferences or workshops to maintain professional knowledge.
rationale: The binding constraint is that attendance itself, including the networking and CE-credit attestation tied to a named individual, cannot be delegated; only the note-taking and summarising slice is machine-substitutable.

dwa_title: Monitor work environment to ensure safety or adherence to specifications.
rationale: Fixed sensors and machine vision cover known hazard classes, but walking a site and noticing unanticipated deviations from spec still needs an on-site, answerable observer.

dwa_title: Analyze forensic evidence to solve crimes.
rationale: Instruments and database matching automate parts of the workflow, but chain-of-custody, admissibility and courtroom testimony legally require an identifiable expert to own every interpretive step.

dwa_title: Design medical devices or appliances.
rationale: Regulatory design-control regimes require a named engineer accountable for risk analysis and verification of a device that can kill a patient, so even excellent AI-generated designs must be owned by a qualified human.

dwa_title: Operate digital imaging equipment.
rationale: Automated exposure and image-processing settings are mature, but positioning the subject or document and physically running the scanner or camera ties the work to a location and a pair of hands.

dwa_title: Confer with clients to discuss treatment plans or progress.
rationale: Treatment planning conferences require therapeutic alliance, consent and clinical responsibility; model assistance is confined to preparation and documentation.

dwa_title: Manage healthcare operations.
rationale: Healthcare operations sit inside licensure, accreditation and patient-safety regimes that require a named administrator or clinical leader to answer for decisions.

dwa_title: Test biological specimens to gather information about patient conditions.
rationale: High-throughput clinical analyzers already automate the assay chemistry, but specimen handling, pre-analytic prep and the licensed sign-off on abnormal or equivocal results keep a certified human in the loop.

dwa_title: Measure distances or dimensions.
rationale: Coordinate measuring machines, laser scanners, LiDAR and machine vision are commercially routine for dimensional metrology; the residual human role is placing or presenting the object, not determining the number.

dwa_title: Train patients, family members, or caregivers in techniques for managing disabilities or illnesses.
rationale: Tailoring disease-management technique to a specific household while handling fear, grief and adherence is irreducibly relational, and a licensed professional must be accountable for the instruction given.

dwa_title: Direct scientific activities.
rationale: Setting research direction and leading scientific staff turns on contested priority judgments and personal authority over a team; AI can draft plans and synthesize literature but cannot own the direction.

dwa_title: Collaborate with law enforcement or security agencies to share information.
rationale: Sharing information with police or security agencies carries legal privacy, evidentiary and safety liability that requires a named accountable person, even though the drafting and matching work is automatable.

dwa_title: Administer screening tests to determine abilities or treatment needs.
rationale: Digital screening instruments can be self-administered and auto-scored, yet eliciting valid responses from children, patients in distress or those with impairments is inherently relational and the resulting treatment decisions require a responsible professional.

dwa_title: Hire farming, fishing or forestry workers.
rationale: Field hiring of seasonal crews happens face-to-face, often informally and under labour-and-immigration compliance rules that demand an accountable employer of record.

dwa_title: Evaluate construction projects to determine compliance with external standards or regulations.
rationale: Code compliance turns on physical inspection of partly concealed work at a site and on a certified inspector's signature that carries structural-safety liability.

dwa_title: Inspect condition of natural environments.
rationale: Satellite and drone imagery automate landscape-scale change detection, but assessing soil, species and habitat condition demands on-the-ground expert observation.

dwa_title: Supervise employees.
rationale: Algorithmic scheduling and performance analytics are widely deployed, but employment law and the relational substance of managing people require a responsible human supervisor.

dwa_title: Coordinate artistic activities.
rationale: Marshalling performers, rehearsals and creative logistics requires on-site presence and real-time interpersonal direction; only the calendaring and logistics paperwork slices off.

dwa_title: Supervise scientific or technical personnel.
rationale: Scheduling, review drafting and progress tracking are assistable, but directing and evaluating staff is an authority relationship in which a named manager must own personnel decisions.

dwa_title: Implement organizational process or policy changes.
rationale: Implementation, as opposed to drafting, is change management: securing buy-in, exercising authority over staff and absorbing resistance, none of which can be delegated to a system that no one reports to.

dwa_title: Communicate with others to coordinate vehicle movement.
rationale: Automated ground-movement and traffic-control aids exist, but responsibility for real-time vehicle separation rests with licensed controllers and spotters because errors are immediate and physical.

dwa_title: Teach medical procedures to healthcare personnel.
rationale: Procedural skill transfer requires supervised hands-on practice and a credentialed clinician who signs off on competence; patient-safety liability cannot be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Measure physical or chemical properties of materials or objects.
rationale: Instrumentation and automated analysers handle the measurement itself, but sample preparation, fixturing and instrument calibration still require hands on the material; the binding constraint is physical sample handling rather than cognition.

dwa_title: Adjust equipment to ensure optimal performance.
rationale: Closed-loop and adaptive control automate parameter tuning where sensors exist, but the generic form covers much hands-on mechanical adjustment with no actuation path.

dwa_title: Coordinate forestry or agricultural activities.
rationale: Weather, biology and equipment variability force on-site judgment and crew coordination; farm-management software optimises scheduling but cannot own the field decisions.

dwa_title: Direct equipment maintenance or repair activities.
rationale: Scheduling and prioritising maintenance is software-assisted, but directing crews on physical equipment requires on-site supervision and a person answerable for safety lockouts and repair adequacy.

dwa_title: Confer with family members to discuss client treatment plans or progress.
rationale: The substance is a negotiated, emotionally charged conversation with a family about care decisions; the relationship and the clinician's accountability for the plan are the work itself.

dwa_title: Collaborate with healthcare professionals to plan or provide treatment.
rationale: The activity bundles joint deliberation with actual treatment delivery, so both licensure accountability and hands-on presence keep it lodged in clinicians.

dwa_title: Calibrate equipment to specifications.
rationale: Calibration against a written spec is rule-bound and increasingly software-driven, yet physical setup and the accountable sign-off keep a technician in the loop.

dwa_title: Operate photographic developing or print production equipment.
rationale: Modern digital print and processing lines run largely on automated cycles, but loading media, chemistry handling, color checks and jam clearing still require a body at the machine.

dwa_title: Monitor animal behavior or condition.
rationale: Precision-livestock sensors and vision systems reliably flag lameness, feeding and estrus in confined settings, yet diagnosing subtle condition changes and handling the animal still requires a stockperson on site.

dwa_title: Inspect equipment to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Built-in self-test and predictive-maintenance analytics automate the checks on modern connected equipment, but most legacy plant still needs a human to look, listen and actuate controls.

dwa_title: Evaluate performance of educational staff.
rationale: Teacher evaluation drives employment decisions subject to union contracts and due process, requiring classroom observation and a named supervisor's accountable judgment.

dwa_title: Diagnose dental conditions.
rationale: Caries and radiograph AI detection is commercially deployed, but diagnosis still needs intraoral examination, tactile probing and a licensed dentist to own the finding.

dwa_title: Create advanced digital images of patients using computer imaging systems.
rationale: Reconstruction and rendering software does the computational work, but acquiring usable images still requires a technologist positioning and reassuring a live patient.

dwa_title: Supervise trainees.
rationale: The binding constraint is the developmental relationship: assessing a novice's readiness, correcting them in the moment and vouching for their competence requires a named human mentor, even though AI can draft curricula and feedback.

dwa_title: Manage agricultural or forestry operations.
rationale: Managing a biological production system spans labour, capital, regulatory compliance and irreversible seasonal bets, so decision support helps but a responsible operator remains the constraint.

dwa_title: Direct surveying activities.
rationale: Survey data capture is heavily instrumented, but a licensed surveyor must direct field crews and certify boundary results with legal liability attached.

dwa_title: Maintain electromechanical equipment.
rationale: Electromechanical servicing couples electrical fault tracing, which models can guide, with physical disassembly and alignment that must be done on site.

dwa_title: Collect data about project sites.
rationale: Site characterisation requires physical presence to observe conditions that remote sensing under-samples, such as subsurface, access and adjacent-use details.

dwa_title: Measure the level or depth of water or other liquids.
rationale: Ultrasonic, float and pressure level sensors with telemetry already replace manual gauging almost everywhere; only initial installation needs a physical presence.

dwa_title: Test characteristics of materials or structures.
rationale: Universal testing machines and NDT equipment run instrumented protocols automatically, but specimen mounting and in-situ structural testing require physical presence.

dwa_title: Mark materials or objects for identification.
rationale: Labelling and marking is already mechanised in high-volume settings via print-and-apply and laser marking systems; the binding constraint is only the physical handling of varied, unstructured items in low-volume or field contexts.

dwa_title: Test fluids to identify contamination or other problems.
rationale: Inline sensors and automated fluid analyzers already do continuous contamination monitoring; the residual human role is drawing samples from equipment in the field.

dwa_title: Create physical models or prototypes.
rationale: Additive manufacturing and CNC already turn digital models into parts unattended, but fixturing, finishing, assembly and hands-on evaluation of the prototype require bodily presence in the shop.

dwa_title: Demonstrate products to consumers.
rationale: Live product demonstration requires physically handling the item in front of an audience and reading their reactions; video substitutes exist but do not replace in-person demos.

dwa_title: Monitor patient progress or responses to treatments.
rationale: Models can synthesise labs, vitals and notes well, but clinical responsibility for interpreting a patient's trajectory and changing treatment is legally vested in a licensed clinician who must also observe the patient directly.

dwa_title: Direct activities of subordinates.
rationale: Algorithmic task dispatch exists and is widely deployed, but directing people carries legal employer authority and motivational weight that cannot be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Test quality of materials or finished products.
rationale: Automated QC stations and vision systems cover repetitive gauging and defect detection, but sampling plans, disposition of borderline lots and certification signatures remain human.

dwa_title: Stock products or parts.
rationale: Warehouse goods-to-person robotics handle replenishment in engineered facilities, but shelf-level stocking of heterogeneous items in retail environments remains a dexterity problem unsolved at scale.

dwa_title: Record images needed to address work issues.
rationale: Someone or something must be physically at the scene with a camera and choose what evidence to capture; fixed cameras and drones automate only pre-arranged viewpoints.

dwa_title: Maintain test equipment.
rationale: Calibration, cleaning, part replacement and functional checks on physical instruments demand dexterous hands-on work in situ; software can schedule and log maintenance but cannot perform it.

dwa_title: Direct green energy production operations.
rationale: Generation plants run under heavy SCADA automation, yet directing the operation entails grid-compliance and safety responsibility plus physical intervention during abnormal events.

dwa_title: Resolve employee or contractor problems.
rationale: Employment grievances and contractor disputes require a trusted, legally accountable human to hear the parties and own the settlement; LLMs can only prep policy analysis and draft language.

dwa_title: Counsel clients or patients regarding personal issues.
rationale: Reading distress, building rapport and adapting to a person's lived circumstances is the substance of the activity; duty of care and disclosure obligations keep a named human in the role.

dwa_title: Inspect condition or functioning of facilities or equipment.
rationale: Condition monitoring sensors and predictive analytics automate a growing share for instrumented assets, but most facility and equipment checks still need a technician on site with eyes and hands.

dwa_title: Inspect equipment or systems.
rationale: Instrumented condition monitoring covers sensored assets, but generic inspection still means physically reaching, opening and sensing equipment that is not wired for telemetry.

dwa_title: Monitor activities of individuals to ensure safety or compliance with rules.
rationale: Camera-based behaviour analytics can flag anomalies, but judging intent, intervening with the person and bearing responsibility for a safety call keeps a human present.

dwa_title: Inspect facilities for cleanliness.
rationale: Judging cleanliness means being physically present, looking under and behind things and sometimes swabbing; sensors and cameras cover only a fraction of the surfaces that matter.

dwa_title: Mediate disputes.
rationale: Neutrality, trust and the capacity to manage emotion between adversaries are the substance of mediation, and legal or professional frameworks require an identifiable, accountable neutral.

dwa_title: Prepare compounds or solutions for products or testing.
rationale: Automated dispensing and formulation systems perform routine weighing and dilution reliably; the binding constraint is physical handling of diverse reagents and hazardous materials plus verification of concentration accuracy.

dwa_title: Measure ingredients.
rationale: Industrial batching and gravimetric dosing systems are fully automated, but the same activity in kitchens, pharmacies and small-batch shops requires manual handling of variable containers and materials that no deployed manipulator handles economically.

dwa_title: Maintain work equipment or machinery.
rationale: Generic hands-on upkeep of heterogeneous machinery; the physical variability of access, fasteners and wear defeats today's robotics even where scheduling and logging are automated.

dwa_title: Supervise technical medical personnel.
rationale: Regulatory frameworks for diagnostic and technical medical services name a qualified supervisor who must vouch for personnel competence and procedure quality.

dwa_title: Direct industrial production activities.
rationale: Production scheduling and line analytics are software-assisted, but directing a plant means on-floor supervision of crews and safety-critical decisions that a named supervisor must own.

dwa_title: Measure ingredients or substances to be used in production processes.
rationale: Gravimetric batching and automated dosing systems are mature, commercially standard equipment; the task is a deterministic measurement against a recipe.

dwa_title: Calibrate scientific or technical equipment.
rationale: Automated calibration routines and drift computation are common, but traceable calibration requires physically connecting standards and a signed certificate from an accredited technician.

dwa_title: Treat chronic diseases or disorders.
rationale: Chronic disease management is heavily information-based and algorithm-assisted, but prescribing authority, longitudinal patient relationship and adherence coaching keep a licensed human accountable.

dwa_title: Counsel clients on mental health or personal achievement.
rationale: Chatbots can deliver structured self-help content, but licensed mental-health counseling requires therapeutic alliance, risk assessment for self-harm and a clinician answerable for the outcome.

dwa_title: Investigate illegal or suspicious activities.
rationale: Investigation blends surveillance, interviewing and discretionary judgment about people's liberty; automated detection supplies leads but not the authority or the situational reading.

dwa_title: Maintain mechanical equipment.
rationale: Lubrication, adjustment and part replacement demand hands on machinery in unstructured settings; sensor-based condition monitoring automates the detection half but not the intervention.

dwa_title: Supervise workers providing client or patient services.
rationale: Overseeing service delivery requires on-the-spot observation of staff-client interaction and intervention authority that cannot be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Inspect facilities or sites to determine if they meet specifications or standards.
rationale: Compliance inspection requires walking the site and a licensed inspector who is legally answerable for the certification, even where drones and checklists assist evidence gathering.

dwa_title: Direct energy production or management activities.
rationale: SCADA and automated dispatch already handle much of the control loop, but licensed operators must remain answerable for grid/plant decisions with catastrophic failure modes.

dwa_title: Supervise medical support personnel.
rationale: Clinical delegation rules and licensure make a specific supervising professional legally answerable for what support staff do to patients.

dwa_title: Test mechanical systems to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Condition-monitoring sensors flag anomalies automatically, but functional run-up checks of mechanical assemblies typically require an operator present to actuate and observe them.

dwa_title: Direct natural resources management or conservation programs.
rationale: Conservation program leadership involves stakeholder negotiation, regulatory accountability and field oversight; models help with monitoring data and plan drafting only.

dwa_title: Treat patients using psychological therapies.
rationale: The therapeutic alliance itself is the active ingredient, and licensure plus suicide/harm risk require a named clinician; chatbots can deliver manualised CBT content but cannot own the case.

dwa_title: Direct healthcare delivery programs.
rationale: Clinical program direction is legally tied to licensed accountability for patient safety and to leading clinical staff, regardless of how much analytics is automated.

dwa_title: Document events or evidence, using photographic or audiovisual equipment.
rationale: Capturing evidence requires a camera physically present at the scene with framing choices made in situ; fixed automated cameras cover only a narrow slice, and chain-of-custody integrity demands a named human.

dwa_title: Distribute promotional literature or samples to customers.
rationale: Mail and fulfilment channels are automated, but handing samples or flyers to people in a store, event or street setting requires physical presence and dexterity no deployed system provides.

dwa_title: Monitor clients to evaluate treatment progress.
rationale: Judging whether a client is actually improving depends on rapport, affect and disclosure within a therapeutic relationship; the evidence is generated by the human contact itself.

dwa_title: Fabricate products or components using machine tools.
rationale: CNC machining with automated tool changers and pallet loading is mature and CAM programming is increasingly model-assisted; setup, workholding, inspection and troubleshooting still bind a machinist to the cell.

dwa_title: Set up laboratory or field equipment.
rationale: Setup means physically arranging, connecting and calibrating varied apparatus in unstandardised spaces; only fully integrated lab-automation cells do this without hands, and field deployment is wholly manual.

dwa_title: Prepare materials for processing.
rationale: Bulk feeding, batching and dosing are heavily automated in continuous process plants, but non-uniform materials and manual loading in smaller operations still require hands.

dwa_title: Represent the organization in external relations.
rationale: Representation is inherently a matter of a person standing for the organization and being answerable for what is said; delegation to a machine defeats the purpose of the role.

dwa_title: Manage construction activities.
rationale: Project management tooling automates cost/schedule tracking, but contractual and safety accountability for the build rests with a licensed or designated manager on site.

dwa_title: Coordinate enforcement of laws or regulations.
rationale: Enforcement discretion and the deployment of officers carry statutory authority and due-process liability that must rest with a named official.

dwa_title: Operate laboratory equipment to analyze medical samples.
rationale: Clinical chemistry and hematology analyzers with track systems already automate the analytic run end-to-end, but specimen integrity checks, instrument QC and the licensure-bound sign-off on results keep a certified technologist in the loop.

dwa_title: Implement therapeutic programs to improve patient functioning.
rationale: Program design and progress tracking are highly model-exposed, but implementation means in-person coaching, motivating and adapting to a patient in real time.

dwa_title: Collect geographical or geological field data.
rationale: Remote sensing, drones and instrumented logging capture much field data automatically, yet outcrop interpretation, sample selection and terrain access still require a geoscientist on site.

dwa_title: Install computer hardware.
rationale: Racking, cabling and seating components demands dexterous hands in a specific room; no deployed robot handles heterogeneous hardware installs, so only the planning and documentation slices are automatable.

dwa_title: Conduct diagnostic tests to determine patient health.
rationale: Sample and image acquisition demand physical presence, and diagnostic conclusions carry licensure liability that requires a named clinician to sign regardless of model accuracy.

dwa_title: Gather physical survey data.
rationale: Data must be captured in situ; drones, LiDAR and GNSS rigs automate parts of the capture but instrument placement, ground truthing and access decisions still need a body on the terrain.

dwa_title: Monitor the handling of hazardous materials or medical wastes.
rationale: Hazardous and medical waste handling is governed by regulations that name a responsible custodian and require physical verification of containment and manifests; tracking software supports but cannot substitute.

dwa_title: Clean objects.
rationale: Industrial parts washers and cleaning machines automate the repetitive cases, but arbitrary objects and surfaces still require dexterous human handling.

dwa_title: Package materials or products.
rationale: High-throughput packaging lines are routinely fully automated; irregular, fragile or low-volume mixed items still defeat deployed grippers, keeping some human packing.

dwa_title: Maintain medical laboratory equipment.
rationale: Modern analyzers self-calibrate and flag faults, but physical servicing, reagent handling and QC verification still require a technologist present and accountable under lab accreditation rules.

dwa_title: Encourage patients or clients to develop life skills.
rationale: Motivating behaviour change in clients hinges on a trusted human relationship and clinical accountability; digital coaching tools supplement rather than replace it.

dwa_title: Dispose of trash or waste materials.
rationale: Automated bin lifts and some warehouse waste handling exist, but general trash collection across unstructured environments still needs human hands and mobility.

dwa_title: Package materials for transport.
rationale: Automated case packers, palletisers and shrink-wrappers are mature commercial technology; the constraint is capital cost and product variety, not capability.

dwa_title: Develop collaborative relationships between departments or with external organizations.
rationale: Trust between organisations is held by named individuals with reputations and reciprocal obligations; software can schedule and draft but cannot be the party to a relationship.

dwa_title: Monitor health or behavior of people or animals.
rationale: Written broadly, this spans wearables-based tracking through direct custodial observation; the in-person duty of care over a living subject is what blocks end-to-end automation.

dwa_title: Supervise production or support personnel.
rationale: Scheduling and output tracking are already software-driven, but on-floor presence, discipline, safety responsibility and employment decisions require an accountable supervisor.

dwa_title: Direct medical science or healthcare programs.
rationale: Clinical and research program leadership carries licensure, regulatory and patient-safety liability that must attach to an identifiable clinician-administrator.

dwa_title: Prepare materials for preservation, storage, or display.
rationale: Handling fragile, unique artifacts or specimens requires in-situ tactile care and case-by-case conservation judgment that no deployed system provides.

dwa_title: Operate precision equipment to control microscopic or nanoscopic processes.
rationale: Nanofabrication and advanced microscopy tools already run scripted, closed-loop recipes, yet alignment, specimen preparation and drift/fault diagnosis keep a skilled operator physically present.

dwa_title: Establish interpersonal business relationships to facilitate work activities.
rationale: The relationship itself is the deliverable, and counterparties extend goodwill to a person rather than to a system, so delegation destroys the value created.

dwa_title: Direct installation activities.
rationale: Supervising installation crews requires presence at the work face to see conditions and redirect workers; only sequencing and documentation are offloadable.

dwa_title: Counsel family members of clients or patients.
rationale: The work is emotionally laden relational support around a patient's condition or crisis; trust, presence and clinical accountability make the human counselor the deliverable, not the information.

dwa_title: Operate laboratory or field equipment.
rationale: Bench and field instruments require physical sample handling, calibration and in-situ placement; lab automation covers only high-volume standardized workflows.

dwa_title: Verify alignment of structures or equipment.
rationale: Laser trackers, total stations and vision metrology already measure alignment automatically, but mounting targets, accessing the structure and interpreting out-of-tolerance causes still need a technician on site.

dwa_title: Maintain clean work areas.
rationale: Floor-scrubbing robots handle open surfaces only; clearing clutter, wiping surfaces and tidying tools require dexterous manipulation in cluttered space that is not commercially solved.

dwa_title: Assist customers to ensure comfort or safety.
rationale: Kiosks and chat agents handle the informational slice, but attending to a patron's physical comfort and safety on site requires a present body able to intervene.

dwa_title: Investigate safety of work environment.
rationale: Safety assessment binds on walking the site, observing actual worker behaviour and signing a regulated finding; sensors and checklist tools inform but cannot bear the statutory responsibility.

dwa_title: Test patient vision.
rationale: Autorefractors, automated visual field testing and retinal AI are commercially deployed, but positioning the patient and confirming refraction subjectively still anchors the task to a present, accountable examiner.

dwa_title: Instruct patients in the use of assistive equipment.
rationale: Fitting and coaching a patient on a walker, prosthesis or lift requires hands-on positioning and real-time safety correction at the bedside, and a licensed clinician is answerable if the patient falls or misuses the device.

dwa_title: Supervise patient care personnel.
rationale: Nursing and care supervision carries direct patient-safety liability and requires physical presence on the unit to assess acuity and reassign staff in real time.

dwa_title: Test patient heart or lung functioning.
rationale: Automated ECG and spirometry interpretation is mature, but attaching leads, coaching patient effort and validating results require a licensed clinician physically present.

dwa_title: Inspect work sites to identify potential environmental or safety hazards.
rationale: Hazard identification is open-ended perception in an unstructured, changing site combined with statutory safety responsibility that must rest on a named competent person.

dwa_title: Cultivate micro-organisms for study, testing, or medical preparations.
rationale: Automated incubators, bioreactors and colony-picking robots handle routine culture work, but aseptic technique across varied media and organisms still relies on trained hands, and contamination or misidentification carries real cost.

dwa_title: Care for plants or animals.
rationale: Irrigation, climate control and automated feeders cover routine slices, but unstructured handling of living organisms in varied environments still needs hands and eyes on site.

dwa_title: Clean facilities or work areas.
rationale: Commercial cleaning robots cover large uncluttered floors but not detail work around fixtures and objects, so human hands remain the binding requirement.

dwa_title: Inspect equipment to ensure safety or proper functioning.
rationale: Safety-critical clearance to operate typically requires a competent person to attest in person; sensors can flag faults but cannot assume the liability for declaring equipment safe.

dwa_title: Stock medical or patient care supplies.
rationale: Automated dispensing cabinets and par-level software cover the tracking layer, but physically restocking varied clinical supplies in occupied care areas, with sterility and expiry checks, stays manual.

dwa_title: Distribute supplies to workers.
rationale: Automated tool cribs and dispensing cabinets exist for high-volume standard items, but general issuing of supplies to workers on a jobsite remains a bodily presence task.

dwa_title: Observe individuals' activities to gather information or compile evidence.
rationale: Fixed-camera analytics can log activity, but covert or mobile observation of a specific person in unstructured environments needs bodily presence, and evidentiary use requires a named observer who can testify to chain of custody.

dwa_title: Inspect areas for compliance with sanitation standards.
rationale: Sanitation inspection depends on in-situ sensory checks (surfaces, temperatures, odours, pest signs) in cluttered, variable premises; enforcement authority and citation liability rest with a named official.

dwa_title: Distribute materials to employees or customers.
rationale: Handing over physical materials to specific people in a specific place is the whole activity; vending, AGV and locker systems automate only narrow, standardised slices of it.

dwa_title: Clean facilities or equipment.
rationale: Clean-in-place systems and floor robots automate specific slices; general cleaning of arbitrary facilities and machines remains a manipulation problem.

dwa_title: Repair medical facility equipment.
rationale: Repair of imaging, monitoring and life-support equipment requires in-situ physical service plus regulated sign-off that a named biomedical technician must provide; AI can only assist fault isolation.

dwa_title: Evaluate patient functioning, capabilities, or health.
rationale: Functional assessment blends observed physical performance with patient report and clinical licensure accountability, none of which a system can own end-to-end.

dwa_title: Follow protocols or regulations for healthcare activities.
rationale: Following clinical protocol is an act of bedside execution under professional licensure; systems can prompt and check adherence but a credentialed clinician must perform and answer for it.

dwa_title: Cultivate land.
rationale: Auto-steer tractors and GPS-guided tillage are commercially real and among the most automated field operations, but supervision, hitching, and field-edge decisions still keep an operator in or near the cab.

dwa_title: Represent the interests of clients in legal proceedings.
rationale: Appearance before a tribunal requires a licensed advocate with fiduciary duty; unauthorised-practice rules and courtroom standing are the binding constraint, not drafting ability.

dwa_title: Test patient hearing.
rationale: Automated audiometry and OAE screening exist and run largely unattended, but otoscopy, fitting transducers and handling unreliable responders require hands-on presence and licensed interpretation.

dwa_title: Examine medical instruments or equipment to ensure proper operation.
rationale: Devices increasingly self-diagnose, but patient-safety regulation requires a biomedical technician or clinician to physically verify and document fitness for use before a device touches a patient.

dwa_title: Fabricate devices or components.
rationale: High-volume fabrication is automated, but the generic activity spans one-off and custom assembly where fixturing, fitting and part variability still require human hands.

dwa_title: Disassemble equipment to inspect for deficiencies.
rationale: Teardown of varied equipment requires dexterous, improvised manipulation and tactile diagnosis; robotic disassembly remains confined to narrow, uniform product lines.

dwa_title: Prepare biological specimens for laboratory analysis.
rationale: Automated stainers, tissue processors and liquid handlers cover high-volume steps, yet grossing, embedding and irregular specimen handling remain manual and specimen mix-ups have patient-level consequences.

dwa_title: Measure radiation levels.
rationale: Fixed area monitors, dosimeter networks and drone-mounted detectors already log radiation continuously without humans, but contamination surveys of specific surfaces and the regulatory sign-off on exposure findings keep a licensed person in the loop.

dwa_title: Prepare biological samples for testing or analysis.
rationale: Track-based clinical lab automation already handles centrifugation, aliquoting and loading end-to-end for standard tubes; non-standard sample types and accessioning exceptions keep humans in the loop under licensure.

dwa_title: Collect samples of raw materials or finished products.
rationale: Automatic samplers on production lines and silos are commercially common, yet lot-by-lot sampling across warehouses, trucks and batches still needs a person walking to the material.

dwa_title: Monitor construction operations.
rationale: Construction sites are unstructured, changing physical environments where spotting unsafe or out-of-spec work requires being present and directing crews; drone and camera progress-capture automates documentation but not the supervisory judgment or safety liability.

dwa_title: Perform animal breeding procedures.
rationale: Estrus detection sensors and genetic-matching software are widely deployed, but insemination and obstetric handling remain manual procedures on live animals.

dwa_title: Treat acute illnesses, infections, or injuries.
rationale: Diagnostic reasoning is highly LLM-exposed, but examination, procedures and prescribing authority require a licensed practitioner physically present and legally answerable.

dwa_title: Repair medical or dental assistive devices.
rationale: Binding constraint is dexterous, highly varied hands-on work on bespoke devices (prosthetics, hearing aids, dental appliances) often fitted to an individual patient; only diagnostic reasoning and documentation are model-exposed.

dwa_title: Adjust tuning or functioning of musical instruments.
rationale: Pitch detection is fully solved by software, but turning pins, voicing and regulating an instrument require skilled hands on the object.

dwa_title: Test facilities for environmental hazards.
rationale: Fixed sensors automate continuous monitoring, but hazard surveys require sampling in specific physical locations and certified inspectors whose names go on the report.

dwa_title: Assemble equipment or components.
rationale: High-volume standardized assembly is robot-automated, but the binding constraint is dexterous manipulation of varied parts and fixtures, which remains uneconomic outside high-volume lines.

dwa_title: Collect evidence for legal proceedings.
rationale: Chain of custody and admissibility require a named, sworn human collector; digital-forensics tooling assists but cannot itself attest to provenance in court.

dwa_title: Survey land or bodies of water to measure or determine features.
rationale: Autonomous survey vessels, multibeam sonar and UAV LiDAR automate data capture on open terrain and water, but mobilising equipment, handling access, weather and obstructed sites still demands a crew in place.

dwa_title: Measure the physical or physiological attributes of patients.
rationale: Automated vitals monitors, kiosks and wearables already capture most physiological measures without a clinician; the residual constraint is positioning the patient and applying sensors correctly.

dwa_title: Collect environmental data or samples.
rationale: Fixed automated sensor stations and autonomous samplers exist for routine monitoring, but most environmental sampling requires travelling to unstructured terrain and physically handling media, which no deployed robot does generally; chain-of-custody signatures add a human anchor.

dwa_title: Collect samples for analysis or testing.
rationale: Inline autosamplers automate sampling on fixed process streams, but generalised sampling requires physically reaching varied locations and choosing representative material.

dwa_title: Clean equipment, parts, or tools to repair or maintain them in good working order.
rationale: Automated parts washers cover batch cleaning, but disassembly and targeted cleaning of varied tools and components is dexterity-bound.

dwa_title: Inspect work environments to ensure safety.
rationale: Safety walkthroughs require being bodily present to notice open-ended, unanticipated hazards and to engage workers; the binding constraint is that a certified inspector's signature carries legal liability for what was missed.

dwa_title: Deliver items.
rationale: Indoor delivery robots and some sidewalk/AV pilots are deployed, but last-metre handoff across varied buildings and recipients still binds humans to the task.

dwa_title: Fit eyeglasses, contact lenses, or other vision aids.
rationale: Automated refraction and lens-ordering software handle the measurement and specification, but physical fitting, adjustment and comfort verification on a person's face or eye require hands and licensed sign-off.

dwa_title: Install instrumentation or electronic equipment or systems.
rationale: Mounting, wiring and calibrating instrumentation in situ demands fine manual work in confined, non-standard spaces; software can only assist with configuration and documentation.

dwa_title: Replace worn equipment components.
rationale: Predictive analytics can say what to replace, but disassembly and refitting of worn parts in confined, variable machinery remains manual outside a few automated tool-change cells.

dwa_title: Teach basic living or other adaptive skills to patients or caregivers.
rationale: Teaching dressing, feeding or transfer skills requires hands-on demonstration, physical guidance and safety oversight in the patient's real environment.

dwa_title: Operate industrial equipment.
rationale: Process control loops automate steady-state running, but setup, changeover, and response to abnormal conditions on industrial plant remain hands-on; the activity is written too broadly for a confident single score.

dwa_title: Practice athletic or artistic skills.
rationale: The activity is the embodied human development of skill itself — the point is that a specific human body improves, so substitution is conceptually impossible even if coaching analytics can assist.

dwa_title: Enforce rules or regulations.
rationale: Detection can be automated, but confronting a person, exercising discretion and bearing legal authority for the enforcement action requires an accountable human.

dwa_title: Assemble mechanical components or machine parts.
rationale: Robotic assembly is fully deployed for high-volume standardised parts, but compliant fitting, fastening and tolerance adjustment in low-volume or complex assemblies still requires human dexterity.

dwa_title: Inspect safety equipment to ensure proper functioning.
rationale: Extinguishers, harnesses, alarms and eyewash stations are dispersed physical items whose inspection is codified as a tagged, signed, legally mandated act by a qualified person.

dwa_title: Apply chemical solutions to plants to protect against disease or insects or to enhance growth.
rationale: Autonomous sprayers and see-and-spray systems are deployed in row crops, but licensed applicator responsibility for pesticide use, drift and dosage keeps a certified human accountable.

dwa_title: Care for animals.
rationale: Animals are unpredictable moving subjects requiring tactile handling and behavioural reading; only feeding, watering and environmental monitoring are reliably mechanised.

dwa_title: Provide care for animals.
rationale: Same binding constraint as general animal care: physical presence and dexterous, responsive handling of a living creature that cannot be standardised.

dwa_title: Adjust settings or positions of medical equipment.
rationale: Positioning equipment relative to a patient's body is embodied and patient-specific, and clinical safety regulation requires a licensed operator to own the setting.

dwa_title: Maintain facilities.
rationale: Heterogeneous hands-on work across unstructured building environments; no deployed robotics handles the variety of tools, access and improvisation involved.

dwa_title: Interact with patients to build rapport or provide emotional support.
rationale: Rapport and emotional comfort with a vulnerable patient is the deliverable itself, and in clinical settings it is expected to come from an accountable present human.

dwa_title: Survey land or properties.
rationale: GNSS, robotic total stations and drone photogrammetry capture the data with little manual effort, but boundary determination requires on-site evidence interpretation and a licensed surveyor's seal that statute assigns to a named individual.

dwa_title: Reassemble equipment after repair.
rationale: Post-repair reassembly is one-off, unfixtured work on worn or non-uniform units; no deployed robotic system handles this variability.

dwa_title: Monitor patients following surgeries or other treatments.
rationale: Telemetry and early-warning scores automate detection, but post-procedure deterioration demands bedside assessment and immediate physical intervention under licensed accountability.

dwa_title: Analyze crime scene evidence.
rationale: Evidence must be recognised, collected and documented in situ under adversarial legal scrutiny; neither the embodiment nor the sworn accountability can be delegated to a system.

dwa_title: Operate farming equipment.
rationale: GPS auto-steer and driverless tractor kits are commercially real but confined to open-field, supervised operations; hitching, implement adjustment and unstructured terrain still demand an operator aboard.

dwa_title: Assemble precision electronics or optical equipment.
rationale: Pick-and-place and automated optical alignment are mature for mass electronics, but low-volume precision optical assembly still depends on human micro-dexterity and tactile feedback.

dwa_title: Monitor patient conditions during treatments, procedures, or activities.
rationale: Intraprocedural monitors already compute and alarm automatically, but standards of care and licensure require a named attendant physically present to interpret and respond within seconds.

dwa_title: Protect wildlife or natural areas.
rationale: Protection is enacted in the field through habitat management, enforcement and negotiation with landowners; sensing and monitoring can be automated but the protective action itself is embodied and legally attributed.

dwa_title: Direct natural resources extraction projects.
rationale: Extraction site direction combines on-site supervision of crews and hazardous equipment with licensed safety and environmental responsibility that regulators pin to a named person.

dwa_title: Prepare medical supplies or equipment for use.
rationale: Sterile processing and tray setup involve manipulating diverse instruments under asepsis rules; automation exists only for washing/sterilizing steps, and a named person verifies sterility.

dwa_title: Direct construction activities.
rationale: Directing construction means live field judgment over crews, subcontractors and unforeseen site conditions, with code and safety liability attaching to the responsible supervisor.

dwa_title: Repair precision devices or workpieces.
rationale: Fine-tolerance diagnosis and manipulation of one-off damaged parts exceeds the fixturing and tactile control of deployed robotic systems.

dwa_title: Assess patient work, living, or social environments.
rationale: Home and workplace assessment requires physical presence and clinical rapport to observe hazards and social context that patients under-report; a licensed clinician owns the resulting care plan.

dwa_title: Install gauges or controls.
rationale: Installing instrumentation happens in cramped, one-off equipment configurations requiring manual mounting, wiring and calibration, and a certified technician typically signs off because faulty controls create safety hazards.

dwa_title: Make patient-assistive devices or device models.
rationale: Custom orthotics/prosthetics fabrication is increasingly aided by 3D scanning and printing, but the binding constraint is bespoke hands-on shaping and fitting to an individual body, which no deployed system does end-to-end.

dwa_title: Maintain medical equipment or instruments.
rationale: Hands-on cleaning, sterilization, calibration and verification of clinical devices, with regulated documentation that a named technician must certify for patient safety.

dwa_title: Administer non-intravenous medications.
rationale: Pharmacy robots and dispensing cabinets automate preparation, but placing oral or topical medication into a specific patient and verifying ingestion remains a hands-on, signed-for act.

dwa_title: Test patient nervous system functioning.
rationale: Neurological examination and electrodiagnostic testing depend on skilled manual technique, patient cooperation and real-time adaptation; signal interpretation is assistable but the exam itself is not.

dwa_title: Operate diagnostic imaging equipment.
rationale: Protocol selection and dose optimisation are increasingly automated, but positioning patients and bearing radiation-safety responsibility keeps a credentialed operator in place.

dwa_title: Provide basic health care services.
rationale: Broad bedside care bundles physical assistance with reassurance and triage judgment; automation reaches only the documentation and guidance layer.

dwa_title: Maintain security.
rationale: Surveillance analytics and access control are heavily automated, yet physical response to incidents and liability for safety outcomes keep a human on post.

dwa_title: Fabricate medical devices.
rationale: Serial medical device manufacturing is already heavily machine-automated, but custom and low-volume fabrication still requires skilled manual work plus regulated quality sign-off.

dwa_title: Testify at legal or legislative proceedings.
rationale: Testimony is sworn by a named individual subject to perjury and cross-examination; no machine can hold that legal standing regardless of how well it could prepare the content.

dwa_title: Prepare medications or medical solutions.
rationale: Robotic IV compounders and pharmacy automation exist, yet physical handling plus licensure-based responsibility for a dose that can kill a patient keeps a named pharmacist or nurse accountable.

dwa_title: Sterilize medical equipment or instruments.
rationale: Autoclaves and washer-disinfectors do the sterilization itself, but loading, inspection, packaging and validated sign-off of sterility remain a human responsibility.

dwa_title: Clean medical equipment or facilities.
